Player of the Match: Édier Ocampo | Western Conference Round One, Game 1 FC DALLAS 3-0 PORTLAND TIMBERS Game 1 in a nutshell After a quiet, cagey first half, FC Dallas (No. 2) revved the engines to secure a 3-0 win over the Portland Timbers (No. 7). With Petar Musa ’s elite playmaking from his No. 9 position and Daniel Job continuing to look like one of the signings of the summer window, the hosts simply outplayed Portland in the biggest moments. Despite exploring a more possession-heavy style this fall, Dallas head coach Eric Quill reverted to his most-used approach in Game 1: defend in a deep block and knife forward on the break. It flourished. Portland, for their part, looked light on attacking difference-makers. Kristoffer Velde had bright moments after a red-hot finish to the regular season, but struggled at times to sneak past Shaq Moore on the left wing. Elsewhere, an injury to Ariel Lassiter in the first half left the Timbers in a pinch. Now, they have a hole to dig out of. WATCH: Joaquín Valiente brace guides FC Dallas to Game 1 victory What to expect in Game 2 When: Saturday, 10:30 pm ET Watch: Apple TV; FS1, FOX Deportes; TSN, RDS Facing a must-win game at Providence Park, Portland will look to take control in Game 2. But with Dallas likely defending deep and attacking in transition, two keys will define whether their season continues. Portland have to be more incisive against Dallas’ defensive shape. If Velde and Vincent Janssen can maximize their touches, and if David Da Costa is more proactive with his passing, the Timbers will cause Dallas more problems on the ball. The Timbers need to be sharper in defensive transition. They simply cannot afford to make mistakes that leave Job and Musa in the open field. If Portland nail those two things, they’ll have a shot at forcing a Game 3. Likelihood of Game 3: Medium. Dallas have the talent edge in this series, but home-field advantage and a couple of difference-makers could see Portland extend the series. Player of the Match: Joaquín Valiente | Western Conference Round One, Game 1 ST. LOUIS CITY SC 3-2 LAFC Game 1 in a nutshell St. Louis (No. 3) looked more like themselves – their true, MLS-record-unbeaten-run selves – in a 3-2 win over LAFC (No. 6) than we'd seen since they won the US Open Cup in late October. With two weeks off after Decision Day, head coach Yoann Damet’s team had a chance to rest, reset and get midfielder Alex Mățan and goalkeeper Roman Bürki back for their playoff run. And so, in front of a tremendous crowd at Energizer Park, St. Louis produced the elite possession play that helped define their regular season. With Mățan roaming, Chris Durkin and Daniel Edelman in a double pivot, and even Conrad Wallem pinching in from right wingback to help overload the midfield, St. Louis had spells of carving through LAFC's defensive structure with ease. The second half, where LAFC twice clawed back from a multi-goal hole, made for a nervy ending. Still, St. Louis put themselves in position to protect the lead and take the series lead. WATCH: St. Louis CITY top LAFC for first-ever playoff win What to expect in Game 2 When: Saturday, 8:30 pm ET Watch: Apple TV LAFC had some positive pressing moments early in Game 1, but those dried up as the match wore on. They didn’t commit enough bodies to the press to truly trouble St. Louis’ possession approach, and they didn’t find their best attacking players early enough. That has to change in Game 2. LAFC will need to be more aggressive, or at least more efficient, on both sides of the ball. With Mățan nursing a slight injury and Carlo Holse missing Game 1, LAFC will have a chance to face a not-quite-fit version of St. Louis. Can they take advantage? Likelihood of Game 3: Medium. We saw precious little of Son Heung-Min in Game 1. The same goes for Denis Bouanga. If those two can get more involved, LAFC will like their chances of forcing a Game 3. If not, we’re looking at a sweep by St. Louis. Player of the Match: Simon Becher | Western Conference Round One, Game 1 SAN JOSE EARTHQUAKES 2-1 HOUSTON DYNAMO FC Game 1 in a nutshell Set pieces fueled San Jose's 2-1 win over Houston. Ronaldo Vieira’s corner-kick finish gave the Earthquakes a 1-0 lead, Eduard Löwen’s spectacular free kick doubled it, and the hosts never looked back. Sure, Houston found a goal via Duncan McGuire's header in the 80th minute, but it was too little, too late. Impressively, head coach Bruce Arena’s team pulled off the victory with a never-before-used starting lineup. With Lowen and Beau Leroux starting ahead of Vieira in midfield, Niko Tsakiris and Timo Werner playing in varied winger roles, and Preston Judd starting up top, it was the strongest collection of talent we’ve seen from the Quakes all season. Houston didn't have the answers on either end, and couldn't climb out of a 2-0 hole. item.title: Doc Rivers gives Miami Heat coach Erik Spoelstra credit for figuring out how to use Giannis Antetokounmpo
item.description: Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images Former Milwaukee Bucks head coach Doc Rivers has heaped praise on Miami Heat head coach Erik Spoelstra for using Giannis Antetokounmpo more efficiently. The two-time MVP is having a brilliant season, averaging 28.2 points, 12.6 rebounds and 5.5 assists. His numbers were consistent even when the Heat were losing games at the start of the season. When the Heat lost their first four games, many analysts pointed fingers at Antetokounmpo and criticised his game. However, the 10-time All-Star has let his performances speak for themselves and his dominance has helped them get on a seven-game winning streak, although he did not play in their recent win against the OKC Thunder. What has changed for the Heat is the way they have been using Giannis. Instead of relying on him, the Heat have finally seen an increase in production from their stars like Bam Adebayo and Klay Thompson. All of this has been designed by Spoelstra, who Rivers has gone up against many times in his career. Doc Rivers explains what Erik Spoelstra is doing different with Giannis Antetokounmpo Antetokounmpo’s numbers have never dipped, despite his team not seeing any success. This includes his time with the Bucks when he was coached by Doc Rivers. Last season, Antetokounmpo’s usage rate was 36.8, which was reflected in his production, as he averaged 27.6 points, 9.8 rebounds and 5.4 assists, while shooting 62.4% from the field. However, this season, his usage rate is down to 32.8, which is the lowest for him since the 2023-24 season. Despite this, he has managed to wreak havoc on defences by making the right plays. “One of the things that Erik is doing a great job of is Giannis is rolling a lot more when he doesn’t have the ball. He is setting picks and he is rolling. I always thought in Milwaukee, when we got him to roll- a Giannis roll- come on, it’s hard. And what Giannis is doing on the roll is he’s getting it if they come; he’s making the plays; if they don’t come, you’re in trouble. He’s off the ball more now, like his usage rate is down, but his quality of play is up,” said Rivers on The Bill Simmons podcast. The Heat are currently leading the league with 120.7 points per game. This is due to how spread out the production is across the board. They now have five players who are scoring 10 points or more, which is what has led to their seven-game winning streak. Their next game is against the Philadelphia 76ers, who are one of the leading contenders in the Eastern Conference. A win against them will be a huge boost to the Heat, but Antetokounmpo’s status for the game is in doubt. Their win against the OKC Thunder is proof that they have the next-man-up mentality, and if the Greek Freak is out, it will be interesting to see how the Heat play against a Philly team, who have stars across the board. item.title: Anger, disappointment must fuel critical fixes for Army football
item.description: Army has backed itself into a must-win contest at Rice University if there is to be a postseason in 2026, and the Black Knights intend to fight for what they think they deserve. The Black Knights (5-5) are mired in a three-game slide, falling to Memphis, Air Force and East Carolina on Saturday in a mistake-prone final home outing, turning a once-promising season into fight for bowl survival. Army has to beat Rice in order to reach the requirement of six wins ahead of the bowl bids going out on December 6. Asked about the team spirits during his press conference on Tuesday, Nov. 24, head coach Jeff Monken said of his team: "They're ticked off, and so am I. And being ticked off can fuel some passion to try to get better. You can mope around and feel sorry for yourself - certainly, that's one option. (But) that's a choice we make." Defensive lineman Dillon Stowers said after Saturday's setback that there's disappointment, but no quit from the team. "What the outside doesn't see is how close everyone is inside the locker room," he said. "Everyone's leaning on each other right now, picking each other up. ... I have no doubt and all the confidence in the world in us to get back out and put our best foot forward." Army opened as a 7.5-point favorite, but the spread has dropped to 5.5 in what is anticipated to be another low-scoring contest, the oddsmakers setting 48.5 points as the over/under. Rice (2-9) had lost nine in a row before winning at struggling Temple last Thursday, and Saturday will be the Owls' final game. The last thing Army wants is to ponder a four-game losing streak headed into two weeks of prep for the Navy game, trying to salvage a .500 campaign against a resurgent Midshipmen team, which followed a 2-6 start with wins over Temple and Memphis and is predominant 16.5-point favorite at Charlotte this Saturday. Army football struggles offensively Only weeks earlier, Army's offensive line was judged as one of the top units in the nation as the Black Knights put up major rushing yardage. But injuries sidelined three starters ahead of the East Carolina game and a fourth went down late in the third quarter. Asked about the team spirits during his press conference on Tuesday, Nov. 24, head coach Jeff Monken said of his team: "They're ticked off, and so am I. And being ticked off can fuel some passion to try to get better. You can mope around and feel sorry for yourself - certainly, that's one option. (But) that's a choice we make." Defensive lineman Dillon Stowers said after Saturday's setback that there's disappointment, but no quit from the team. "What the outside doesn't see is how close everyone is inside the locker room," he said. "Everyone's leaning on each other right now, picking each other up. ... I have no doubt and all the confidence in the world in us to get back out and put our best foot forward." Army opened as a 7.5-point favorite, but the spread has dropped to 5.5 in what is anticipated to be another low-scoring contest, the oddsmakers setting 48.5 points as the over/under. Rice (2-9) had lost nine in a row before winning at struggling Temple last Thursday, and Saturday will be the Owls' final game. The last thing Army wants is to ponder a four-game losing streak headed into two weeks of prep for the Navy game, trying to salvage a .500 campaign against a resurgent Midshipmen team, which followed a 2-6 start with wins over Temple and Memphis and is predominant 16.5-point favorite at Charlotte this Saturday. Army football struggles offensively Only weeks earlier, Army's offensive line was judged as one of the top units in the nation as the Black Knights put up major rushing yardage. But injuries sidelined three starters ahead of the East Carolina game and a fourth went down late in the third quarter. The impact resulted in a season-low 180 yards of rushing and total offense of only 264 yards (second worst to the 220 posted a week earlier against Air Force). Senior left guard Kyle Kloska is done for the season, Monken confirmed on Tuesday. Left tackle Henry Appleton was close to being ready for East Carolina, but the coaches decided not to rest him. All-American center candidate Brady Small was injured against Air Force and watched from the sidelines on Saturday, wearing a protective boot and using a coaster to support his leg. Right guard Paolo Gennarelli got hurt against the Pirates, visited the medical tent and was spotted afterward trying to test his mobility but did not return. That left right tackle Teddy Williams as the lone healthy starter. In place of the injured linemen were Xavier Archawski, Ben Britton, Chuck Johnson and Jonah Zimmerman. Monken said Tuesday he was hopeful for the return of Appleton, Small and Gennarelli, but mid-week statements and posted depth charts have not always lined up with starts. Monken went into a long explanation about the resulting problems, essentially saying some gaps for running backs are not being pried open wide enough at times, or gaps aren't being closed for attacking linebackers and blitzing safeties. "We just didn't do it well enough, consistently enough," he noted. He also mentioned some outside runs were clipped short on heel tackles, and some option reads were probably mistaken. "There's things like that, throughout the course of the game that we've got to improve, get better at and execute more effectively," he said. As for the continuity between the existing backs and basically a new cast of linemen, he said no matter who's playing, there's got to be a trust factor that the calls are being executed properly. "There's a lot of things that can take a play the wrong direction," Monken said. The Black Knights and Owls will kick off at 2 p.m. ET, 1 p.m. CT on Saturday, Nov. 28. The announcers are LaDarrin McLane and Smacker Danielson. The Army football radio network features WBNR (1260-AM, 96.5-FM), WLNA (1420-AM, 94.3-FM) and WGHQ (920-AM, 92.5-FM). The game can also be heard on The Varsity app, Knight Vision website and Sirius XM 252 (Army) and 264 (Rice). The Army network has Rich DeMarco, Dean Darling, sideline reporter Tony Morino and host Joe Beckerle on the radio call. John Minko co-hosts the pregame show. The Rice radio announcers are J.P. Heath and Nate Griffin. item.title: Victor Wembanyama faces untimely injury concern before showdown with Luka Doncic
item.description: Victor Wembanyama faces untimely injury concern before showdown with Luka Doncic originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Victor Wembanyama has spent the opening weeks of the NBA season making a compelling case to win his first MVP award. The San Antonio Spurs superstar has delivered some enormous individual performances while helping his team emerge as one of the league's most dangerous contenders. However, an untimely injury concern has introduced some uncertainty entering Thanksgiving weekend. Wembanyama missed Monday's 123-107 victory over the Sacramento Kings because of back tightness and is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Portland Trail Blazers , according to Reuters. While the Spurs demonstrated their impressive depth against Sacramento, basketball fans have another reason to closely monitor Wembanyama's availability. A highly anticipated meeting with Luka Doncic and the Los Angeles Lakers awaits Friday. Two superstars are separating themselves The NBA's latest official MVP Ladder, published last week, placed Doncic first and Wembanyama second. Miami Heat superstar Giannis Antetokounmpo occupied the third spot, but Friday's game could provide an early opportunity for the two leading candidates to make statements against each other. Victor Wembanyama (back) listed questionable for Wednesday. — Underdog NBA (@UnderdogNBA) November 25, 2026 Wembanyama is averaging 29.9 points, 12.3 rebounds and 3.9 blocks this season. He recently produced separate performances of 50 and 52 points, illustrating just how dramatically his offensive capabilities have developed. His ability to influence games defensively while delivering enormous scoring totals makes his emergence particularly remarkable. Perhaps equally impressive is San Antonio's 15-3 record. Wembanyama's individual production is translating into victories, an important consideration when evaluating legitimate MVP candidates rather than simply identifying the league's most productive players. item.title: Imesha Dulani, Sathya Sandeepani star as Sri Lanka beat Ireland to win Women's Emerging Nations Trophy
item.description: Sri Lanka produced a commanding all-round performance to defeat Ireland by six wickets and clinch the ICC Women's Emerging Nations Trophy 2026 on Wednesday. Imesha Dulani starred with an unbeaten 44 as Sri Lanka comfortably chased down the 97-run target in just 12.4 overs in the final at the Karwan Sports Club. The victory marked Sri Lanka's first title in the tournament's history, succeeding Thailand, who won the inaugural edition in 2025. Sri Lanka's bowlers bundle out Ireland for 96 After opting to bat first, Ireland endured a disastrous start, losing captain Gaby Lewis in the opening over at 5/1. The early setback soon turned into a collapse as they slipped to 10/2 before struggling to recover. Sri Lanka's disciplined bowling attack kept the pressure firmly on Ireland, reducing them to 54/6 inside 12 overs. Alana Dalzell emerged as Ireland's top scorer with 24 off 25 deliveries, while Louise Little contributed 15 off 17 balls. Georgina Dempsey also chipped in with 13, but Ireland failed to build meaningful partnerships and were eventually bowled out for 96 in 19.3 overs. Sathya Sandeepani was the standout performer with the ball, claiming four wickets for just 13 runs in her four overs. Kavisha Dilhari, Sugandika Kumari, Nimasha Meepage and Chethana Vimukthi picked up a wicket apiece, while two run-outs further dented Ireland's innings. Imesha Dulani guides Sri Lanka to title Chasing 97, Sri Lanka made an aggressive start but suffered a brief setback after Sanjana Kavindi departed for 25 off 22 balls. Captain Harshitha Samarawickrama was dismissed for a golden duck on the following delivery, leaving Sri Lanka at 35/2. Ireland attempted to stage a comeback through Kia McCartney and Cara Murray, who picked up two wickets each to reduce Sri Lanka to 69/4 in the ninth over. However, Dulani held her nerve and ensured there were no further hiccups. She remained unbeaten on 44, while Dilhari provided valuable support with an unbeaten 16 off just 10 deliveries. The pair stitched together an unbroken 30-run partnership to take Sri Lanka to 99/4 in 12.4 overs, sealing a convincing six-wicket victory and the championship trophy. Brief Scores Ireland Women: 96 all out in 19.3 overs (Alana Dalzell 24, Louise Little 15; Sathya Sandeepani 4/13) lost to Sri Lanka Women: 99/4 in 12.4 overs (Imesha Dulani 44*, Sanjana Kavindi 25; Kia McCartney 2/16, Cara Murray 2/38) by six wickets.

Brief Scores Ireland Women: 96 all out in 19.3 overs (Alana Dalzell 24, Louise Little 15; Sathya Sandeepani 4/13) lost to Sri Lanka Women: 99/4 in 12.4 overs (Imesha Dulani 44*, Sanjana Kavindi 25; Kia McCartney 2/16, Cara Murray 2/38) by six wickets.

item.title: Browns’ home-field advantage could be on display on Sunday Night Football vs. the Raiders
item.description: The dedication of the Cleveland Browns fan base has been a huge advantage for the players on the field throughout the team’s history. The fans do a great job of cheering the team on while also making it a challenging environment for opposing teams. The Browns are 4-0 at home so far this season, and the team had a game-winning fourth-quarter drive in each of those victories. While on-field performance is certainly the main factor in these wins, it cannot be overlooked that the atmosphere at Huntington Bank Field played a role in the team’s ability to finish these games strong. Consistency at home can build confidence too and help to establish a winning culture. When fans recognize that the atmosphere makes a difference and players are confident that it gives them an extra edge, it can have a positive impact on the team’s performance on the field. With four home games left against the Las Vegas Raiders, Cincinnati Bengals, Atlanta Falcons, and Indianapolis Colts, Cleveland hopes to finish out the season 8-0 in front of the home crowd. Let me know what you think in the comments – Is Cleveland’s home field advantage a real factor? Join the conversation! item.title: Exeter defender Harper 'honoured' by Kenya cap
item.description: Vincent Harper is on a season-long loan at Exeter City from Walsall [Shutterstock] Vincent Harper says he relished the chance to play for Kenya during the international break. The Exeter City wing-back, on loan from League Two rivals Walsall, came on in his country's 2-1 Africa Cup of Nations qualifier loss to South Africa in Nairobi last week. It was his second cap this season, having played 90 minutes against Rwanda in a friendly last month. "It's a massive honour," Harper told BBC Radio Devon. "My parents were both born there, it just feels almost like you're repaying back, not to them but also to the whole country. "It's a lot of pressure at the same time, but overall it's just a big honour." Harper has played 13 times since returning to Exeter this season - he had a two-year spell at St James Park before he joined Walsall in the summer of 2025. The former Bristol City youth player made his English Football League debut when he moved to Exeter from Eastleigh in 2023 and went on to play 65 times in all competitions before moving to the Midlands. "I think it just shows you the next level or the level you need to be at to play consistently at an international level," he added. "It's very intense and very quick and you're playing with the best of the best of the country so you've got to definitely be at your 'A' game. "If you make one mistake then you'll definitely be punished." Exeter City bring in Harper and Samuel on loan Harper started all seven of Exeter's games after arriving back at the club. But while he was away on international duty in October, Exeter hit a rich vein of form and he has not been able to get back into the starting line-up. He is hopeful he can force his way back into a side that has been one of League Two's in-form teams over the past two months - Exeter have risen from close to the relegation zone to the brink of the play-off places after just one loss in their past 10 games in all competitions. "It's a bit of a frustrating one," he admitted. "Before the first internationals I was heavily involved and then the boys started doing well while I was away. "It's nice to see the boys doing well, but I want to be more part of it and spend more time on the pitch and show them what I can do. "But overall it's good to see the team winning and although I might not get as many minutes as I want, it's nice to come on here and there and play my part as well." item.title: Pep Guardiola confirms he will coach a national team next as USMNT fans hope for return to management in USA
item.description: Pep Guardiola confirms he will coach a national team next as USMNT fans hope for return to management in USA originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The greatest manager of this generation has already been mulling the avenue for his return. Pep Guardiola has been out of a job since departing Manchester City in the summer, and while it seems he's enjoying his time off, he has clearly been thinking about where he wants to end up next. It would be a first for Guardiola, who has never managed internationally before, but he has many national federations on high alert. Most notably, the U.S. national team has reportedly made Guardiola its top choice, and will likely spend the remainder of 2026 hoping to either convince him to take the job immediately, or develop a pathway for him to take it when he's ready. If Guardiola is going to take over the USMNT, this was a promising first step towards that eventuality, even if a small one. MORE: All the latest USMNT news | Was Pochettino a success with the USMNT? Pep Guardiola says his next job will be with a national team Speaking with his former Barcelona teammate Romario on his YouTube channel RomarioTV , Pep Guardiola confirmed that his next role will be in international football. When asked if there was a club he would like to coach that he hasn't, Guardiola interjected. "A national team, which is my next step," he said. The 55-year-old has never coached internationally before. He confirmed during the interview that he was approached by the Italian federation (FIGC) over the summer, but turned down the opportunity because he wanted to take time off and had only just departed Man City. "I spoke with them," Guardiola said of the FIGC. “It was an honor. I even feel bad or ashamed to say no to a country like Italy. It is one of the biggest honors I’ve had that they thought of me as the right man to manage Italy. But they found me in a moment when I needed to stop. "If they had come in one or two years time, probably I would have taken it." MORE: USMNT 2027 schedule, fixtures, dates, competitions, and more Could Pep Guardiola coach the USMNT? There is a real pathway for Pep Guardiola to coach the United States men's national team, if he wants it. Mauricio Pochettino, who departed last week to take over at Manchester United , has laid the groundwork for another top manager like Guardiola to take over in his wake. The manner of Pochettino's departure will surely put other top managers on high alert. The Argentine was highly emotional at his exit press conference, saying that the choice to leave was "the most difficult decision of my career" and speaking extremely well of the federation and staff he worked alongside. Speaking through tears, Pochettino said that the federation "made me feel really happy doing my job, sharing an amazing project, being part of this family." Pep Guardiola says his next job will be with a national team Speaking with his former Barcelona teammate Romario on his YouTube channel RomarioTV , Pep Guardiola confirmed that his next role will be in international football. When asked if there was a club he would like to coach that he hasn't, Guardiola interjected. "A national team, which is my next step," he said. The 55-year-old has never coached internationally before. "I spoke with them," Guardiola said of the FIGC. “It was an honor. I even feel bad or ashamed to say no to a country like Italy. It is one of the biggest honors I’ve had that they thought of me as the right man to manage Italy. But they found me in a moment when I needed to stop. "If they had come in one or two years time, probably I would have taken it." MORE: USMNT 2027 schedule, fixtures, dates, competitions, and more Could Pep Guardiola coach the USMNT? There is a real pathway for Pep Guardiola to coach the United States men's national team, if he wants it. Mauricio Pochettino, who departed last week to take over at Manchester United , has laid the groundwork for another top manager like Guardiola to take over in his wake. The manner of Pochettino's departure will surely put other top managers on high alert. The Argentine was highly emotional at his exit press conference, saying that the choice to leave was "the most difficult decision of my career" and speaking extremely well of the federation and staff he worked alongside. Speaking through tears, Pochettino said that the federation "made me feel really happy doing my job, sharing an amazing project, being part of this family." Pochettino's efforts in the United States may not have brought tangible growth on the pitch in terms of results, but he elevated the program's culture and built a much larger player pool from which to choose possible starters. Additionally, there is time to work out something with Guardiola. The Spaniard has said multiple times he wishes to take a full year off from management. To that end, there is just one singular international break between Pochettino's departure at the end of the November window and the start of the CONCACAF Gold Cup in the summer — an interim boss could be named to handle the CONCACAF Nations League finals in the March window before Guardiola takes over in June. This would give Pep time to enjoy the remainder of his hiatus, while also having the certainty of knowing what his next job will be, allowing both him and the federation to prepare for his eventual start date. Guardiola also has an affinity for the United States. As Sporting News reporter Dom Farrell put it , "Guardiola lived in New York during his 2012/13 sabbatical and is enamoured with U.S. sporting culture, especially basketball. He became good friends with Boston Celtics coach Joe Mazzulla during his time at City." There is still a very long way to go in this regard, and Guardiola's level of interest in the role is still unknown. But the fact he has not publicly turned it down yet indicates he probably thinks there is at least some level of realistic future between the two.

item.title: How the Miami Heat saved the season after a terrible start
item.description: (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Heat ended last season in an awkward spot. For the fourth straight year, they found themselves in the NBA Play-In Tournament. Unfortunately, this was the first time they couldn’t make it out. They have a S-Tier leading man calling the shots, a battle-tested defensive anchor , and a culture of winning in the ugliest ways possible. Their roster, while nothing special, was far from the dregs of the association. It contained a good blend of young bucks and proven veterans. If the injury gods smiled in their favor and a couple of prospects took meaningful steps forward, the Heat could have run it back and flirted with 50 wins. And with their knack for upsets, maybe a postseason series victory would have followed. However, the Heat, like the Minnesota Timberwolves , remembered that they didn’t come to the table to nickel and dime their way through the nights. In Miami, they play for keeps. Win big, or go bankrupt trying. So, when Giannis Antetokounmpo finally became available, the Heat swung for the fences – trading the farm in the hopes that the singular excellence of the former two-time MVP , coupled with Bam Adebayo and the scrapes that remained would be enough to vault the team into true contention. Through nine games, it looked like they would be filing for Chapter 7. The Heat were 3-6 and floundering, while their contemporaries (the Detroit Pistons, Boston Celtics, and Philadelphia 76ers) were thriving out the gate. But fast forward to today, and it looks like the big bet they placed may have been the right call. What Changed For The Miami Heat? After their 10-point win over the depleted Oklahoma City Thunder, the Heat are winners of their last seven games and now sit at No. 6 in the Eastern Conference – fully within striking distance of the conference’s upper echelon. In a team sport like basketball, it’s foolish to point to one variable as the reason for positive change, as so many factors contribute to success, but it is hard not to watch this team and look at the ring leader as the catalyst: Erik Spoelstra. Spoelstra may be the best coach in basketball. Heck, he may be one of the five best coaches that ever lived (we know he’s at least one of the top 15 ). Spoelstra is innovative enough to turn oranges into lemonade. No, that’s not a typo that was missed by my editor. The creative lens Spoelstra is able to analyze the game through literally defies everything we know about the human experience. With an average age of 28.8 years old , the Heat have the second-oldest team in the NBA (behind only the Golden State Warriors). item.content:encoded: (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Heat ended last season in an awkward spot. For the fourth straight year, they found themselves in the NBA Play-In Tournament. Unfortunately, this was the first time they couldn’t make it out. They have a S-Tier leading man calling the shots, a battle-tested defensive anchor , and a culture of winning in the ugliest ways possible. Their roster, while nothing special, was far from the dregs of the association. It contained a good blend of young bucks and proven veterans. If the injury gods smiled in their favor and a couple of prospects took meaningful steps forward, the Heat could have run it back and flirted with 50 wins. And with their knack for upsets, maybe a postseason series victory would have followed. However, the Heat, like the Minnesota Timberwolves , remembered that they didn’t come to the table to nickel and dime their way through the nights. In Miami, they play for keeps. Win big, or go bankrupt trying. So, when Giannis Antetokounmpo finally became available, the Heat swung for the fences – trading the farm in the hopes that the singular excellence of the former two-time MVP , coupled with Bam Adebayo and the scrapes that remained would be enough to vault the team into true contention. Through nine games, it looked like they would be filing for Chapter 7. The Heat were 3-6 and floundering, while their contemporaries (the Detroit Pistons, Boston Celtics, and Philadelphia 76ers) were thriving out the gate. But fast forward to today, and it looks like the big bet they placed may have been the right call. What Changed For The Miami Heat? After their 10-point win over the depleted Oklahoma City Thunder, the Heat are winners of their last seven games and now sit at No. 6 in the Eastern Conference – fully within striking distance of the conference’s upper echelon. In a team sport like basketball, it’s foolish to point to one variable as the reason for positive change, as so many factors contribute to success, but it is hard not to watch this team and look at the ring leader as the catalyst: Erik Spoelstra. Spoelstra may be the best coach in basketball. Heck, he may be one of the five best coaches that ever lived (we know he’s at least one of the top 15 ). Spoelstra is innovative enough to turn oranges into lemonade. No, that’s not a typo that was missed by my editor. The creative lens Spoelstra is able to analyze the game through literally defies everything we know about the human experience. With an average age of 28.8 years old , the Heat have the second-oldest team in the NBA (behind only the Golden State Warriors). That is bad news bears in today’s game – one that rewards athleticism, pace, and physicality. Spoelstra realized it was time to demote the veterans that most coaches would remain beholden too. His biggest change was taking Andrew Wiggins (31 years old), and putting Pelle Larsson in his place (25). And when he’s been hurt, instead of reverting back to Wiggins, Spoelstra simply plugs in Myron Gardner (25) in his place. A former second rounder and undrafted player in the place of a former first overall pick, NBA champion, and the third-highest paid player on the team’s payroll. Wiggins wasn’t the only casualty. Bobby Portis’ minutes are down, and Tim Hardaway Jr. is basically out of the rotation entirely. Along with Larsson and Gardner, those minutes are being eaten up by the youthful vigor of second round rookie Ryan Conwell (22). Despite hearing 36 names called before his on draft night, Conwell is seventh among rookies in minutes per game (26.2) in their last seven games. Delegating hustle duties to fresher legs lessens the burdens on Antetokounmpo, Adebayo, Klay Thompson, and Davion Mitchell’s shoulders, and enables them to focus more energy on scoring the ball. The Heat’s effective field goal percentage is up 4.8% over the last seven games. Spoelstra has also made a key strategic shift. To start the season, the Heat were doing a lot of hard hedging with ball screens involving their bigs. The idea is that since they start two center-sized players, they could afford for one of them to play these actions more aggressively, since the other one would be there to clean it up. The idea wasn’t a bad one, in theory, but playing this way asks the three guys not involved in the action to do a lot of flying around to cover up the gaps. Antetokounmpo, now in Year 14, has a lot of tread on his tires, and scrambling around possession after possession isn’t necessarily high on his list of priorities. So, instead of trying to fit a square peg into a round hole, Spoelstra scrapped the idea and started switching everything (except actions involving Portis, which the Heat continue to hedge). This asks Antetokounmpo and company to do a lot less rotating around, and it still lets the Heat benefit from their twin tower configuration (when one of them is switched onto the perimeter, the other can still lurk around the painted area). As a result, the Heat are forcing fewer turnovers (the tradeoff of playing a less aggressive style). However, by switching everything, it is easier for them to keep the ball in front of them, and so the Heat’s opponents are shooting far worse from the floor than they were before. And again, it conserves more energy, so the Heat have their legs under them on their own shots. Due to the constraints of the written medium, we can’t dissect ALL of Spoelstra’s game-changing tweaks, but here are a couple of other developments you can see his fingerprint on: convincing Antetokounmpo into operating more off-the-ball, squeezing the last ounce of magic out of Thompson, and gradually helping mold Mitchell from bust to baller. How Good Are The Heat Actually? The good news for the Heat is that there are some aspects that will improve with time. Despite rostering Antetokounmpo and Adebayo – who have 11 All-Defensive Teams between the two of them – Miami is currently 24th in defensive rating. The adjustments the Heat have made with minute allocation and scheme have helped bump them from 26th in this category in their first nine games to 17th in the last seven, but they are still being hurt by some bad luck. This season, the Heat are surrendering a whopping 45.6% on wide open threes (per NBA.com). That is 2.7% than the next highest team, and 6.1% higher than the league average. The Heat under Spoelstra tend to give up more threes in order to prioritize protecting the rim, but defense has nothing to do with how well opponents shoot on open looks. That’s just luck. If/when that number regresses to the mean (no team has allowed higher than 43% on these shots for an entire season), Miami’s defensive rating will automatically improve. Unfortunately, the Heat have also been the beneficiary of some good luck. According to Estimated Plus-Minus, they have had the third-easiest strength of schedule. They have also lost the fourth-fewest dollars to player injuries (per Spotrac). Antetokounmpo and Thompson have only missed one game each. Mitchell and Adebayo have been available for every game. What happens if one or two of those guys is out for an extended stretch? This isn’t a super deep team. More than likely, the conflicting noise between their negative shooting luck and positive schedule/injury history thus far is a wash. To me, the pace this Heat are currently on (51 wins) seems about right. They are a good team that, even with Spoelstra’s magic touch, still has some glaring flaws (on-ball creation, offensive variety, depth) in a conference filled with them. If they draw the first round opponent or injuries cause them to fall into the play-in tournament for the fifth straight year, another early exit could be in their future. But if Spoelstra keeps putting on a coaching clinic in the best league on the planet and Antetokounmpo can stay healthy enough to match him for a whole postseason, maybe, just maybe, the Heat can return to the NBA Finals for the first time

item.title: ‘Sesame Street for people paying rent’: the viral Instagram series teaching us how to be better adults
item.description: Life100 has racked up hundreds of thousands of followers and millions of views on Instagram by exploring important life lessons It is, unfortunately, a familiar scene. At the dinner table, a woman berates her granddaughter with invasive, personal questions – why are you still single? When are you going to have kids? – punctuated by unnerving thrusts of her steak knife. The granddaughter is clearly uncomfortable, but her grandmother pays no attention. Anyone who has been in this situation likely knows what comes next. The granddaughter may try to deflect, only to invite further questioning, or call out her grandmother’s rudeness, which risks escalation. Continue reading...

item.title: Konga Yakata: Bigger Black Friday Deals, Free Delivery & a Chance to Win an SUV
item.description: With Black Friday arriving on Friday, November 27, Konga is urging shoppers to take advantage of the remaining days of its annual Yakata shopping festival, which ends on November 30. The e-commerce giant is promising exciting deals, significant price reductions, a chance to win a brand-new SUV and free delivery for eligible shoppers in Lagos. Konga Yakata has continued to attract shoppers with discounts across technology, electronics, home appliances, personal care and everyday essentials. However, Black Friday is expected to be one of the biggest highlights of this year’s campaign, with customers encouraged to shop early and take advantage of the offers while stocks last. Speaking on the Black Friday campaign, Irfan Vayani, Senior Vice President at Konga Group, said: “Konga Yakata Black Friday is more than just a sales event; it is our way of giving back to Nigerians who have made Konga their trusted shopping partner. This year, we are going bigger and better. From unbeatable discounts across all categories to the chance to win a brand-new SUV simply by shopping on the Konga app, our goal is to make this Yakata season one of joy, value and transformation. We want to touch lives in real, tangible ways.” Adding more value to the shopping experience, Konga has introduced free delivery for the remainder of Yakata. The offer is available exclusively to shoppers in Lagos who purchase products carrying the KongaNow tag. Eligible customers can therefore enjoy discounted prices while saving on delivery costs, making their Black Friday shopping even more rewarding. Shoppers also stand a chance to win a brand-new SUV through Konga’s Win A Car campaign. Customers who make purchases through the Konga app automatically qualify for the random draw, regardless of the amount spent. There is no minimum purchase requirement, giving every eligible app shopper an opportunity to participate. The festival also features attractive offers from leading brands, including Samsung, LG, Anker, Midea, Starlink, ASUS, Zinox, Guinness and others. Their participation has expanded the range of deals available, giving customers more opportunities to shop across different product categories. Beyond the website and app, Konga has extended the Yakata experience to Instagram and Facebook through interactive live shopping shows. These sessions allow shoppers to discover featured products, enjoy special live deals and engage with the campaign in real time. With the November 30 deadline fast approaching, shoppers have just a few days left to take advantage of the offers. Although some customers have called for an extension, no extension has been announced. The remaining days present an opportunity to secure great deals, enjoy free delivery on eligible Lagos orders and participate in the Win A Car campaign. This Black Friday, shoppers can make their purchases count by visiting the Konga website or app and taking advantage of Yakata before the festival closes on November 30. With the sale

item.title: Jack Harvey named Special Advisor at Dreyer & Reinbold, will sit out 2027 Indy 500
item.description: Motorsport photo IndyCar driver and FOX Sports reporter Jack Harvey has announced that he will step aside from competing in the 2027 Indianapolis 500, shifting his focus toward a return to the cockpit in 2028. The update comes roughly six weeks after the 33-year-old Briton first revealed in mid-October that he had been diagnosed with cancer , a point at which he still hoped to be on the grid in St. Petersburg and race in May. While stepping back from driving duties next year, Harvey will remain closely tied to Dreyer & Reinbold Racing as a Special Advisor while continuing his broadcast work alongside his colleagues at FOX. In a statement shared on social media, Harvey explained the reasoning behind his decision: “Preparing for the Indianapolis 500 requires daily dedication, consistency, and an unwavering commitment. It is a responsibility I have never taken lightly, and I have the utmost respect for the Indianapolis Motor Speedway, the race itself, DRR and my fellow competitors. “As I look to 2027, I recognize I won’t be able to dedicate myself to preparing for the 111th Indianapolis 500 at the level I expect and that this incredible event demands. With that in mind, I’ve made the decision to step aside from competing in 2027 and will focus on preparing for the 2028 event. “While I won’t be behind the wheel, I’m excited to continue my relationship with Dreyer & Reinbold Racing in a new role as Special Advisor. This team has shown me tremendous support and has worked tirelessly both on and off the track. I look forward to returning that same commitment as they make their return to full-time IndyCar competition. “2027 is shaping up to be an incredible year for our sport. The momentum is real, and I can’t wait to reunite with my colleagues at FOX and get back to work.” Dreyer & Reinbold Racing also issued a statement supporting Harvey’s recovery and welcoming him into his new role with the organization: “Jack has been an incredible part of our team and family. His health and well being will always come first. We look forward to supporting Jack’s continued recovery and look forward to seeing him back behind the wheel. In the meantime, we’re excited to welcome Jack into his new role as Special Advisor, where his experience, perspective and passion for the sport will be invaluable as we continue to build toward the future.” Read Also: IndyCar adds Kansas Speedway to 2027 schedule in joint NASCAR weekend IndyCar driver and Fox Sports reporter Jack Harvey announces cancer diagnosis To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: Travis and Jason Kelce say there’s an ‘insane’ rule in the NFL they now want changing
item.description: Photo by David Calvert/Getty Images for American Century Investments Roger Goodell has a good relationship with Travis and Jason Kelce, having already featured on one of their podcasts in the past. This could provide them with the ideal gateway to vent their frustrations with the NFL over the crackback block ruling. There are aspects of a crackback block that are legal, but players can also be penalised for it if not performed to the league’s guidelines. Travis Kelce is a player who will have the crackback block in his arsenal of plays on the field. The tight end has, however, hit out at the NFL for overprotecting players who do not have possession of the football during a game. Travis and Jason Kelce call for NFL to make the crackback block fully legal The crackback block can be a huge advantage to an offense if pulled off correctly, but players are risking a penalty against their team. This is something that the Kelce brothers feel needs looking into by those in charge of the NFL. “You’re running scot-free on the kickoff. You’ve got to have your antennas up. This is why crackbacks should be legal, because guys just have to be on your P’s and Q’s. Keep your head on a swivel, man. You’re on the field,” said Travis on the New Heights podcast. https://open.spotify.com/embed?uri=spotify%3Aepisode%3A1fdxz4celqmI6CnK4BjWfT Jason: “The idea that you’re defenceless when you’re running on the field is insane to me, the ball carrier isn’t right there. You’re not extending for a catch, you’re not throwing a ball, you’re just running, why is there not an onus on defending yourself?” “It’s the dumbest rule change of all time, I hate it.” Travis Kelce has already questioned the NFL’s Hawk-Eye system , with the Kansas City Chiefs’ tight end not pleased with the new technology being introduced into the game. The crackback block is certainly not something new, but the brothers are both keen for a change to the rule. The pair clearly enjoy the physical side of the game, but the NFL are keen to provide as much protection to its players in this day and age due to the new studies showing the impact the game has had on the brains of former players. Read more: Ian Rapoport explains what he knows about Steelers benching Aaron Rodgers Dan Orlovsky insists Aaron Rodgers does not deserve to be benched after Steelers make QB change ‘I don’t really ever…’ – Dak Prescott praises Philadelphia Eagles star he is excited about after unlikely rise

item.title: Geno Auriemma’s UConn matches unfortunate program record seen only once this century
item.description: Geno Auriemma’s UConn matches unfortunate program record seen only once this century originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Geno Auriemma has sounded the alarms with his UConn team -- and the Huskies' season is only seven games old. With Thanksgiving looming, maybe Auriemma and the Huskies will be happy not to see one another for a few days. The holiday will come after Tuesday night's 65-56 defeat to the top-ranked South Carolina Gamecocks at Mohegan Sun Arena, in which the Huskies missed 14 of 20 layups and allowed an uncharacteristic 16-0 Gamecocks run at the end of the second quarter that ultimately decided the game. "I've never had a team at the University of Connecticut that misses this many layups or has (as) many stupid fouls as this team," Auriemma said after Tuesday's loss. "So all you're doing is hurting yourself." UConn off to its joint-worst start this century The Huskies fell to 4-3 with Tuesday night's defeat in Uncasville. That matches the worst start for Auriemma's storied program since the 2023-24 season. Before that, the Huskies had not started a season this slowly since 1986, when Auriemma was beginning his second season at the school. UConn went on to miss the tournament that season and the one after before kickstarting its prolonged run of dominance in the sport. "It's just a very, very, very immature team, basketball-wise," Auriemma said. "And maybe in general, I don't know." “Maybe it's just too much for them. … Maybe I overstated what kind of team we had mentally.” Geno Auriemma did not hold back on the state of UConn basketball Tuesday night. The Huskies are off to their worst start in 40 years. https://t.co/1232ggX82b — Meghan L. Hall (@ItsMeghanLHall) November 25, 2026 It's true that this is a young UConn team. Last year's Huskies relied on the sharpshooting and veteran leadership of eventual No. 1 draft pick Azzi Fudd; the year before, Paige Bueckers was in her last year of NCAA eligibility and signed off with a championship. This UConn team has only two seniors -- and one, KK Arnold, did not play Tuesday. The Huskies' unquestioned best player is a junior. But after that, UConn's second-best player thus far is freshman guard Jovana Popovic. Maybe Auriemma has a point -- this Huskies team needs time to gel and mature. They have a few months to do so before the NCAA Tournament, and the legendary head coach's "tough love" approach has paid dividends before. But as it stands, UConn will require a significant turnaround to reach the heights that Auriemma has long expected of his program. More news: Geno Auriemma’s ominous comments reveal deep problems at UConn after South Carolina loss Sophie Cunningham has curious JuJu Watkins advice after WNBA draft lottery Notre Dame’s Hannah Hidalgo wants to be the No. 1 pick — and so far, she’s making her case

item.title: Could Aaron Rodgers demand his release? 1 team should be all-in on him
item.description: Aaron Rodgers’ future with the Pittsburgh Steelers suddenly looks uncertain after the veteran quarterback was informed that he would be benched for NFL Week 12. Stunner: The Steelers are benching Aaron Rodgers and naming Mason Rudolph the starting quarterback for Friday’s game against the Broncos. Sources say this was a coach’s decision. But Rodgers has struggled and now Mike McCarthy is making a change. https://t.co/wPSeMX3lmq — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) November 25, 2026 The decision to turn to Mason Rudolph for the Black Friday matchup against the Denver Broncos raises questions about how Rodgers will respond and whether he wants to remain in Pittsburgh. If the situation leads to a release, there is one AFC team that should seriously consider pursuing him: the New England Patriots. MORE: Bold predictions for Week 12 of 2026 NFL season Rodgers’ benching could lead to questions about his future in Pittsburgh Nov 22, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers (8) leaves the field after the game at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Late Tuesday night, Rodgers was informed that he would be replaced by Rudolph for the Steelers’ Week 12 matchup against Denver. The situation took another interesting turn Wednesday morning when Rodgers did not show up at the Pittsburgh facility . That naturally raises questions about whether Rodgers intends to stick around after losing his starting job. At this stage of his career, being moved to the bench could change how he views his future with the organization, especially with the season entering a critical stretch. Rodgers has performed better than expected this season, putting up respectable numbers despite having limited offensive talent around him. While Pittsburgh has decided to make a change at quarterback, there is still a case to be made that Rodgers could help another team looking for an upgrade at the position. If Rodgers decides he no longer wants to remain in Pittsburgh, requesting his release could become a possibility. Whether the Steelers would grant that request is another question, but a potential separation would immediately create interest around the veteran quarterback. Their chances of winning the AFC East may be gone, but they remain in the hunt for an AFC Wild Card spot. The biggest problem is the quarterback position. Drake Maye is expected to be unavailable for the foreseeable future, leaving New England in a difficult position as it tries to remain competitive. Without Maye or a significant upgrade at quarterback, the Patriots could have a difficult time keeping their postseason hopes alive. Rodgers would give New England an experienced option capable of providing stability at quarterback. Considering how he has performed this season despite the limitations around him in Pittsburgh, the Patriots could view him as an opportunity to improve their chances of staying in the playoff race. Of course, a potential move would depend on Rodgers becoming available and the Patriots showing interest. But if he does demand his release and the Steelers grant it, there should be a conversation between Rodgers and New England. item.title: Do the Royals need more starting pitching depth?
item.description: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - SEPTEMBER 25: Bryce Miller #50 of the Seattle Mariners pitches during the second inning against the Los Angeles Angels at T-Mobile Park on September 25, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Olivia Vanni/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Royals made it clear that adding starting pitching was a priority this offseason. After finishing second in baseball with a 3.55 ERA for their starting pitchers in 2024, the Royals fell to sixth-worst in the league at 4.58 this year. Thirteen different pitchers made a start, as the Royals were plagued with injuries. J.J. Picollo told reporters he planned to be aggressive in acquisitions after a disappointing 2026 campaign. He followed up by trading All-Star third baseman Maikel Garcia to Seattle in a six-player trade for starting pitchers Bryce Miller and Logan Evans, and reliever Jose Ferrer. The additions of Miller and Evans give the Royals more options in the rotation, but how much have they really improved their depth? The Royals have several pitchers who could factor into the starting rotation in 2027, but there are questions about the health, durability, and track records of many of them. Let’s take a look at the candidates and where they fit. The locks Michael Wacha was the team’s most dependable starter in 2026, an All-Star and a workhorse who led the American League with 200.2 innings. The 35-year-old has been a remarkably consistent presence in the rotation since joining Kansas City, arguably one of their best free agent signings ever. He finished last season strong with a 2.66 ERA in 13 starts after the All-Star break, and the Royals are hoping he can continue that performance into the last year of his contract. Bryce Miller was really terrific in 2024, but has a 4.82 ERA in 209 innings in the two seasons combined since then. He battled elbow issues in 2025, then missed the first six weeks of this season with an oblique injury. The Royals are banking on him being healthy and returning to the form he showed in 2024 when he posted the eighth-lowest ERA in baseball . He has the potential to miss bats – his 24.3 percent strikeout rate that year would have ranked third-best in Royals history, behind only Cole Ragans in 2024 and Zack Greinke in 2009. Noah Cameron figured something out after he began calling his own pitches in July. From July 24 on, he had a 2.58 ERA in 12 games, the 11th-lowest in baseball over that time. He began throwing his cutter more, improving the success of all his pitches. He is the definition of a ‘crafty lefty,’ and while he may not have overpowering stuff, his ability to mix pitches and keep hitters guessing makes him a valuable part of the rotation. Seth Lugo raised alarm bells with a 6.62 ERA over his last 17 starts, the second consecutive year his numbers have gone off the rails in the second half of the season. item.content:encoded: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - SEPTEMBER 25: Bryce Miller #50 of the Seattle Mariners pitches during the second inning against the Los Angeles Angels at T-Mobile Park on September 25, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Olivia Vanni/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Royals made it clear that adding starting pitching was a priority this offseason. After finishing second in baseball with a 3.55 ERA for their starting pitchers in 2024, the Royals fell to sixth-worst in the league at 4.58 this year. Thirteen different pitchers made a start, as the Royals were plagued with injuries. J.J. Picollo told reporters he planned to be aggressive in acquisitions after a disappointing 2026 campaign. He followed up by trading All-Star third baseman Maikel Garcia to Seattle in a six-player trade for starting pitchers Bryce Miller and Logan Evans, and reliever Jose Ferrer. The additions of Miller and Evans give the Royals more options in the rotation, but how much have they really improved their depth? The Royals have several pitchers who could factor into the starting rotation in 2027, but there are questions about the health, durability, and track records of many of them. Let’s take a look at the candidates and where they fit. The locks Michael Wacha was the team’s most dependable starter in 2026, an All-Star and a workhorse who led the American League with 200.2 innings. The 35-year-old has been a remarkably consistent presence in the rotation since joining Kansas City, arguably one of their best free agent signings ever. He finished last season strong with a 2.66 ERA in 13 starts after the All-Star break, and the Royals are hoping he can continue that performance into the last year of his contract. Bryce Miller was really terrific in 2024, but has a 4.82 ERA in 209 innings in the two seasons combined since then. He battled elbow issues in 2025, then missed the first six weeks of this season with an oblique injury. The Royals are banking on him being healthy and returning to the form he showed in 2024 when he posted the eighth-lowest ERA in baseball . He has the potential to miss bats – his 24.3 percent strikeout rate that year would have ranked third-best in Royals history, behind only Cole Ragans in 2024 and Zack Greinke in 2009. Noah Cameron figured something out after he began calling his own pitches in July. From July 24 on, he had a 2.58 ERA in 12 games, the 11th-lowest in baseball over that time. He began throwing his cutter more, improving the success of all his pitches. He is the definition of a ‘crafty lefty,’ and while he may not have overpowering stuff, his ability to mix pitches and keep hitters guessing makes him a valuable part of the rotation. Seth Lugo raised alarm bells with a 6.62 ERA over his last 17 starts, the second consecutive year his numbers have gone off the rails in the second half of the season. He had the seventh-lowest strikeout rate among qualified starters, and while he has never been one to miss bats, it leaves him little room for error. The 37-year-old is entering the last year of his contract (assuming the Royals decline his $17 million option for 2028), and the question is how much he has left in the tank. Rotation candidates Randy Dobnak resurrected his career with the Royals this year after pitching in just six MLB games over the previous three seasons combined. In his first 10 games he posted a 1.92 ERA, only faltering at the end to finish at 3.51. It was the second-best ERA by any Royals starter, but there are questions about how sustainable his performance was. After he joined the rotation on July 2, he had the fifth-lowest strikeout rate in baseball. Tony Gonsolin was signed late in the year and pitched in just one game, but the Royals picked up his $2.5 million option for next year to get a look at what he can do. The 32-year-old right-hander was an All-Star with the Dodgers in 2022, but injuries have derailed his career since then. He missed all of 2024 following Tommy John surgery, then made just seven starts in 2025 before undergoing another elbow procedure involving an internal brace. He’s a decent reclamation project, but the Royals shouldn’t be counting on him at this point considering his injury past. Daniel Lynch IV will get a look as a starter after excelling in the bullpen the last two seasons. Lynch made ten starts late in the year with an unimpressive 6.53 ERA and a very low strikeout rate of 12 percent. He was also a starter from 2021-22, and posted a 5.32 ERA in 42 starts over that time. J.J. Picollo said the Royals recognize the difficulty of transitioning back to a starting role late in the season after having success in the bullpen, but that “he does believe he can start, and we think he did enough over the last two months to compete for a spot in the rotation.” Lynch will get that opportunity in spring training, but the Royals will have to weigh whether he’s better suited to the bullpen, where he has become a valuable weapon. Injured Luinder Avila showed some promise as a starter with good horizontal movement, but walks were an issue. He got hurt late in the year and had Tommy John surgery and will miss all of next season with the hope he can return in 2028. Ryan Bergert looked like a potential rotation candidate going into the 2026 season, but was shelved after just three minor league starts. He also had Tommy John surgery, but could be a candidate to return in the second half. Bergert gets strong strikeout numbers with a high-spin fastball and a slider with good break, but will need to keep the walks down. Stephen Kolek found success with the Royals with a very low walk rate and a lot of groundballs. He doesn’t miss many bats at all, but he shows good command and terrific pitch efficiency. He had Tommy John surgery late in the year and is unlikely to return at all in 2027. Ben Kudrna is a Kansas City native who ranked high on team prospect lists until he took a step back in the upper minors in 2025. After one minor league start this year, he had olecranon stress fracture surgery and missed the remainder of the season. He should return this year, but the team will likely slowly ease him back. He will turn 24 in January and if he returns to the high-strikeout pitcher he showed in the lower levels, he could be a factor. John Means is another local boy who had some success with the Orioles, earning an All-Star appearance in 2019. He has pitched in just ten big league games since 2021, missing time with two Tommy John surgeries. He ruptured his Achilles in 2025 as he attempted to come back, and returned to pitch in five minor league games for the Royals. The lefty is 33 years old now, but if he can stay healthy, he could be in the mix for a rotation spot. Cole Ragans has the highest upside of anyone on this list as an All-Star in 2024 who finished fourth in Cy Young voting. Over the last three seasons combined, only five starting pitchers in baseball with at least 200 innings pitched have a higher strikeout rate than his 31.3 percent. He made just eight starts this year before landing on the Injured List with a UCL injury that required surgery, although not Tommy John surgery. He could return in the second half of next year, and the Royals will need him to eventually get back to his All-Star level. Depth options Lucas Braun was acquired from Atlanta in the Lane Thomas trade at the deadline last summer. The 25-year-old right-hander finished 2026 with a 4.16 ERA and 120 strikeouts in 132 innings across Double-A and Triple-A. item.title: ‘Legends never truly die’ – May Edochie mourns father-in-law Pete
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye May Edochie, the estranged wife of Pete Edochie’s son Yul, has mourned the veteran actor, calling him “an institution” whose legacy will live on. In a glowing tribute shared on Instagram on Wednesday, May recalled that false reports of the veteran actor’s death had circulated over the years, but he had continued working. Pete’s family announced that he died in Enugu at 12:30 a.m. on Wednesday, aged 79, after a prolonged battle with prostate cancer. “For so many years, every year, someone somewhere makes a false announcement of your death but you kept going with strength to continue working,” she wrote. View this post on Instagram A post shared by May Yul-Edochie (@mayyuledochie) Reflecting on his death, May said: “One moment, there is life; the next, eternity calls. Such is the fragility of human existence. We make plans, hold conversations, nurse expectations and believe there will always be another day, until life reminds us that tomorrow is never promised.” Calling him the “Lion of Africa,” she said his passing reminded her that “beyond all, the opinions, the misunderstandings and the stories that life sometimes throws around, we are all humans, and death has a way of reminding us of what truly matters.” May also said she would remember Pete as a veteran whose name, voice, presence and contributions to Nollywood would remain unforgettable. “You were an institution, a father figure to many and a man whose legacy will outlive his earthly years,” she wrote. “One thing is certain: legends never truly die; they live on through the memories they create and the impact they leave behind.” She also prayed for Pete’s wife, Josephine, and other relatives, writing: “To mummy and the rest of us you have left behind, may the good Lord strengthen through Christ our Lord.” She ended the tribute with prayers for the deceased: “God rest your soul Ononenyi!” Vanguard News The post ‘Legends never truly die’ – May Edochie mourns father-in-law Pete appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Kremlin declines comment on reports 700,000 Russian soldiers killed in Ukraine war
item.description: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov on Wednesday declined to comment on reports in Russian and international news outlets that around 700,000 Russian soldiers have been killed in the Ukraine war so far. The reports were based on hacked data from Russia's official statistics agency. Peskov said only the defence ministry can disclose figures and told reporters "not to pay attention to any other data".

item.title: My finances were better before Tinubu’s tenure – Seyi Law
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Nigerian comedian, Seyi Law, has admitted that his personal finances were in a better state before President Bola Tinubu assumed office, despite defending the administration’s economic policies and urging Nigerians to endure the hardship associated with them. The comedian made the remarks during an appearance on the Charity Zone Podcast, where he argued that the benefits of some government policies might take years to become evident. Seyi Law, a known supporter of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), said economic policies often come with immediate difficulties before producing long term gains. Using China as an example, he said the country’s emergence as a major global economy involved significant sacrifices. “For China to be where they are today, if they tell you the number of Chinese who died, you won’t believe,” he said. When asked whether Nigerians must die before enjoying the benefits of the country’s economic policies, the comedian clarified that people would have to experience the hardship resulting from such decisions before the expected gains could materialise. “No. You must feel the pain of the policy to reap the benefit of it. Every good policy that becomes good stabilises after 10 to 12 years,” he said. Despite his defence of the government, Seyi Law acknowledged the economic difficulties facing many Nigerians, admitting that people were struggling to afford basic necessities. “People are hungry. I will be a hypocrite, a bad person to say people are not hungry,” he said. He also spoke about how the rising cost of living had affected his ability to support family members living in the United Kingdom. According to him, an amount that previously covered their needs now requires a significantly higher sum, forcing him to increase his financial support. “My finances were better before this government came in. My family are in the UK and then with N1.2 million they are okay, but now I have had to double that to like N4.5 million every other month,” he added. The post My finances were better before Tinubu’s tenure – Seyi Law appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Guardiola says next coaching job will be with national team
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Pep Guardiola says he will manage a national team when he returns to coaching after turning down an offer to take charge of Italy because he felt he needed a break from football. In an interview reported by Reuters, Guardiola told his former Barcelona teammate Romario that he had spoken with the Italian Football Federation but was not ready to take another job. “It was one of the greatest honours I’ve had, that they thought of me to coach Italy. But it came at a time when I needed to stop,” he said. “If it had happened a year or two earlier, I probably would have accepted.” The Spaniard said the approach came when Paolo Maldini and Leonardo, whom he described as people he loved dearly, reached out to him. He added that he did not know how long his break would last. “Right now I feel very well,” Guardiola told former Brazil forward Romario. “But if I return to football one day, it will be when my stomach tells me it’s the right time.” Guardiola left Manchester City at the end of last season after a decade in charge. He won six Premier League titles, including four in succession, three FA Cups, five League Cups and the Champions League. In the same interview, Guardiola said Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo’s rivalry helped prolong both players’ careers. The pair won a combined 13 Ballon d’Or awards and dominated football for more than a decade, including during their spells at Barcelona and Real Madrid. “If Messi hadn’t had Cristiano, or if Cristiano hadn’t had Messi, their careers would likely have been shorter,” Guardiola said. “They had each other in their rearview mirrors, watching what the other was doing made them think: ‘I want to be better than him, I want to win more than him,’” Guardiola, who coached Messi for four seasons at Barcelona, credited the forward for much of his success there. He led the Spanish club to 14 trophies, including two Champions League titles and three La Liga crowns. “Messi! When you have such good players, you become good yourself,” Guardiola said when asked what helped him win so many titles. The post Guardiola says next coaching job will be with national team appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Watch How Whalefall Brought Its Visceral Whale Stomach Survival Thriller to Life
item.description: The star of this year's Resident Evil adaptation endured another horrific experience in the thriller Whalefall in October, which put actor Austin Abrams inside the belly of a 60-ton sperm whale in a fight for survival. While that situation sounds harrowing in real life, filming scenes simulating being inside a whale's stomach also looks exhausting. In a new exclusive clip from Whalefall , viewers get a peek behind the scenes at what Abrams experienced , as more than a dozen stomach puppeteers recreated the visceral action of being digested — all while your host is being attacked by killer whales.

item.title: The unexpected joy hiding in Grand Theft Auto VI’s chaos? A little routine
item.description: Rockstar’s latest blockbuster makes the everyday business of shopping, working out and taking care of a pet snake as compelling as its shootouts and car chases I knew I’d need many skills during the opening hours of Grand Theft Auto VI, but effective time management was not one of them. From playing the previous five titles in the series (and their many spin-offs), I understood I’d have to master Rockstar’s idiosyncratic approach to car handling. True enough, the vehicles do drive like airbeds tied on top of supermarket trolleys. I also knew I’d need to get to grips with the somewhat tricky aiming and shooting if I was to commit any sort of respectable crime spree. But for the first few hours of playing this staggeringly large and bewildering game, what concerned me most was lead character Jason’s personal routine. Each day, he needs to get up, choose an outfit, complete a workout, feed his pet snake Dolores, and perhaps do some DIY, so that when his girlfriend Lucia gets out of jail she’ll fall for him again – rather than fall through his apartment’s rotten staircase. Meanwhile, his drug-smuggling boss phones every five minutes with new parcels for Jason to pick up or drop off, and his pals Cal and Donnie get into all sorts of cocaine-related hijinks they expect Jason to extricate them from. There are also predatory neighbours to do favours for, and groceries to buy. I’ve seen so many people on social media posting about how they took several days off work to play this game, only to find themselves busier and more productive than ever. On his radio show last week, James O’Brien derided himself for completing, in Jason’s apartment, a simple DIY task that he’s put off for months in his own home. I know where he’s coming from. Continue reading...

item.title: Satellites watch volcanic eruptions add new beaches on Iwo Jima | Space photo of the day for Nov. 25, 2026
item.description: null Iwo Jima on Oct. 26, 2026 on the left and the same location on Nov. 11, 2026 shows the impact of a volcanic eruption. (Image credit: NASA Earth Observatory images by Michala Garrison, using Landsat data from the U.S. Geological Survey ) Iwo Jima looks remarkably different from space after a volcanic eruption created new land extending the Japanese island's beaches. What is it? On Oct. 27, Japan's Meteorological Agency detected an underwater volcanic eruption off the shores of Iwo Jima. Soon after this initial detection of the "submarine" volcano, satellites orbiting our planet started taking a look, observing to see what havoc this eruption might wreak. When you compare the satellite images above captured by the Landsat 9 satellite's Operational Land Imager (OLI), you can see the stark differences between the island on October 26 before the eruption and weeks later on November 11. The island was also observed by NASA's NISAR spacecraft as well as the MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer) and VIIRS (Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite) sensors. Together, this imagery gave researchers a more complete picture of how the eruption continued and the effects it left behind. And amazingly, with satellite imagery experts have been able to show that the eruption has actually added more land to the island's beaches. Why is it incredible? On Nov. 16, Japan's Coast Guard confirmed in a statement that about 125 acres (50 hectares) of new land is now connected to the island's southeast beach following the recent volcanic eruption. This is not the first time that a volcano has created new land. Lava and ash from a volcanic eruption can solidify and accumulate, adding land material around the volcano or to a nearby coast if it is located offshore or underwater, as we saw in this case. But these new landforms aren't always permanent fixtures. This new addition to the island's beach could easily and quickly be washed away by the waves, which happened on Iwo Jima just a few years ago in 2023 . And experts expect the same thing to happen with this new land. "I imagine we'll see this new land wash away within a few months," Daniel Slayback, a scientist at NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center who has previously studied landforms created by volcanic eruptions, said in a statement . "But we'll have to wait and see."

item.content:encoded: null Iwo Jima on Oct. 26, 2026 on the left and the same location on Nov. 11, 2026 shows the impact of a volcanic eruption. (Image credit: NASA Earth Observatory images by Michala Garrison, using Landsat data from the U.S. Geological Survey ) Iwo Jima looks remarkably different from space after a volcanic eruption created new land extending the Japanese island's beaches. What is it? On Oct. 27, Japan's Meteorological Agency detected an underwater volcanic eruption off the shores of Iwo Jima. Soon after this initial detection of the "submarine" volcano, satellites orbiting our planet started taking a look, observing to see what havoc this eruption might wreak. When you compare the satellite images above captured by the Landsat 9 satellite's Operational Land Imager (OLI), you can see the stark differences between the island on October 26 before the eruption and weeks later on November 11. The island was also observed by NASA's NISAR spacecraft as well as the MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer) and VIIRS (Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite) sensors.
