item.title: Most Nigerians support political violence when opponents are victims — Shehu Sani
item.description: Former Kaduna Central Senator, Shehu Sani, has accused Nigerians of condoning political violence when it is directed at opponents, warning that the attitude is fuelling attacks on political supporters across the country. Sani said many Nigerians encourage violence against people whose political choices or opinions differ from theirs, rather than condemn such acts irrespective of the victims’ affiliations. He stated this on X on Wednesday following the campaign violence that reportedly left four persons dead in Delta State. Condemning the killings, Sani said Nigerians were more likely to support or excuse political violence when those attacked belonged to opposing political camps. “The political violence in Delta State has led to the death of four supporters of Senator Omo Agege of the NDC. A condemnable act. However, we are shying away from the truth that most Nigerians are fully in support of political violence as long as the victims are in the opposite camp,” he wrote. He argued that people who support violence against political opponents often fail to recognise that such acts could eventually affect their own side. “Most people encourage and support mob or thuggish acts against those they differ with in political choices or opinions. Those aiding and abetting political violence are feeding a Tiger with the thought that it will only consume their political adversaries,” Sani said. The former senator also criticised the media’s handling of reports of political attacks, accusing some media organisations of using descriptions that downplay the severity of violence depending on the political affiliation of those involved. He cited reports of attacks involving former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar in Kebbi and President Bola Tinubu in Abuja, saying some media outlets used different descriptions for incidents involving the two political figures. “Some media Houses have even crafted a beautiful way of reporting political violence…POLITICAL THUGS attacked Atiku in Kebbi while ANGRY YOUTHS attacked Tinubu at Abuja Mosque,” he added. Sani’s comments come amid growing concerns over political violence and intolerance ahead of the 2027 general elections, with incidents involving political supporters raising questions about the safety of campaign activities and the role of political parties in preventing attacks. The post Most Nigerians support political violence when opponents are victims — Shehu Sani appeared first on Vanguard News .

Kober (NASA/Catholic University of America) An expanse of stars gleams in a rainbow of colors in these NASA Hubble Space Telescope images of the Milky Way. The images focus on an area of sky toward the galactic bulge, a densely packed, spherical region of stars that surrounds the center of a galaxy’s disk. These Hubble observations are part of a survey that will help researchers better interpret upcoming Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope observations as they seek to characterize the stars and search for exoplanets in this busy region of our galaxy. Astronomers study the Milky Way’s galactic bulge because it holds nearly a quarter of the galaxy’s stellar mass, and its proximity allows them to examine the region in greater detail. Although we can see the glow from these crowded spheres of stars in other galaxies, they are too jam-packed and far away to resolve individual stars. By studying the Milky Way’s galactic bulge, researchers hope to find new planets and better understand how galaxies form, evolve, and interact over billions of years. Credits: NASA, ESA, and S. Terry (University of Maryland); Image Processing: G. Kober (NASA/Catholic University of America) An expanse of stars gleams in a rainbow of colors in these NASA Hubble Space Telescope images of the Milky Way. The images focus on an area of sky toward the galactic bulge, a densely packed, spherical region of stars that surrounds the center of a galaxy’s disk. These Hubble observations are part of a survey that will help researchers better interpret upcoming Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope observations as they seek to characterize the stars and search for exoplanets in this busy region of our galaxy. Astronomers study the Milky Way’s galactic bulge because it holds nearly a quarter of the galaxy’s stellar mass, and its proximity allows them to examine the region in greater detail. Although we can see the glow from these crowded spheres of stars in other galaxies, they are too jam-packed and far away to resolve individual stars. By studying the Milky Way’s galactic bulge, researchers hope to find new planets and better understand how galaxies form, evolve, and interact over billions of years. Teeming with stars in a rainbow of colors, this NASA Hubble Space Telescope image will help researchers interpret future Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope data of the same region. NASA, ESA, and S. Terry (University of Maryland); Image Processing: G. Kober (NASA/Catholic University of America) Hubble views the universe primarily in ultraviolet, visible, and near-infrared light, while Roman collects data in near-infrared light and some visible light. Because researchers wish to compare Hubble’s observations to future Roman observations, Hubble looked at the region in wavelengths that overlap with Roman’s areas of sensitivity, the red end of the visible spectrum and near-infrared wavelengths. Hubble’s high resolution allows its instruments to collect data on the brightness, ages, composition, and motion of stars over time. With this knowledge, astronomers can search for potential exoplanets, determine the location of black holes or dark matter, and better understand our galaxy’s environment and evolution. A crowded starfield appears interrupted by a dark patch of sky in this NASA Hubble Space Telescope image. A closer look at this darker region reveals many faint stars filling the area. The image is part of a Hubble survey of the galactic bulge. It will help researchers interpret future Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope data of the same region. NASA, ESA, and S. Terry (University of Maryland); Image Processing: G. Kober (NASA/Catholic University of America) A key component of Roman’s future observations is the search for exoplanets by capturing microlensing events , a type of gravitational lensing that occurs when light from a more distant object is magnified and distorted by the mass of a closer object along the line of sight. The way light from the distant star is distorted and magnified can reveal clues to the nature of the foreground star and any planets it may have. Hubble’s observations will help characterize stars in the region before they undergo a lensing event. Months or years in the future, when Roman captures a microlensing event, researchers can compare Hubble data to Roman data of the event, making it easer to interpret. These microlensing events are on a much smaller scale, that of stars and planets, than larger gravitational lenses that occur around galaxies and galaxy clusters . NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope’s high resolution reveals individual stars in an area near our galaxy’s center swarming with stars. The image is part of a Hubble survey of the galactic bulge that will help researchers interpret future Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope data of the same region. NASA, ESA, and S. Terry (University of Maryland); Image Processing: G. Kober (NASA/Catholic University of America) Over Hubble’s lifetime, it has observed our galaxy’s central bulge many times. These legacy surveys include the WFC3 Galactic Bulge Treasury Program that used Hubble’s Wide Field Camera 3 to study the brightness, precise positions, and motions of stars in this congested part of our galaxy. It also includes the Sagittarius Window Eclipsing Extrasolar Planet Search (SWEEPS) that used Hubble’s Advanced Camera for Surveys to look at 180,000 stars in the bulge of our galaxy. These new observations come from an observing program (# 17776 : S. Terry) designed to aid Roman in its search for exoplanets, black holes, neutron stars, and more. The data also adds to Hubble’s continuing legacy of high-precision observations of stars in the galactic bulge. item.title: 10 phones with the fastest charging speeds in 2026
item.description: By Aniobi Angel Smartphone manufacturers are continuously improving charging technology, introducing devices that can recharge their batteries in significantly less time. From 120W ultra-fast charging systems to more moderate fast-charging options, several smartphones now offer features designed to reduce the time users spend connected to power outlets. In 2026, brands such as Xiaomi, Huawei, OnePlus, ASUS, Motorola, Samsung, Google and Apple continue to compete in the development of faster and more efficient charging technology. Here are 10 smartphones with impressive charging capabilities. Xiaomi Redmi Note 14 Pro+ 5G – 120W The Xiaomi Redmi Note 14 Pro+ 5G leads the list with its 120W HyperCharge technology. The smartphone features a 5,110mAh battery and supports ultra-fast wired charging, allowing users to recharge their devices in approximately 20–30 minutes under suitable conditions. Xiaomi 11T Pro 5G – 120W Another Xiaomi device making the list is the Xiaomi 11T Pro 5G, which features 120W Xiaomi HyperCharge technology. Its 5,000mAh battery is designed to support rapid charging, with the manufacturer claiming that the device can reach a full charge in approximately 17 minutes under controlled conditions. OnePlus 15 – 100W The OnePlus 15 features 100W fast-charging technology in markets where the higher-wattage version is available. Its charging system is designed to provide quick battery replenishment, making it suitable for users who depend heavily on their smartphones throughout the day. Huawei Pura 80 Ultra – 100W Huawei’s Pura 80 Ultra offers 100W wired SuperCharge technology and up to 80W wireless charging. The device combines its fast-charging capabilities with a large battery, providing users with both wired and wireless charging options. OnePlus 11 5G Dual SIM – 100W The OnePlus 11 5G supports 100W SUPERVOOC charging in compatible markets. It features a 5,000mAh battery and is designed to recharge quickly, with OnePlus advertising a full charge in approximately 25 minutes under suitable conditions. ASUS ROG Phone 5s 5G Dual SIM – 65W The ASUS ROG Phone 5s is equipped with 65W HyperCharge technology. Designed primarily for mobile gaming, the smartphone combines its high-performance hardware with a 6,000mAh battery and fast-charging support. Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra – 45W Samsung’s Galaxy S25 Ultra supports 45W wired fast charging. The device features a 5,000mAh battery and can reach approximately 65 per cent charge in 30 minutes when used with a compatible 45W adapter. Motorola Razr 50 Ultra 5G – 45W The Motorola Razr 50 Ultra 5G supports 45W TurboPower wired charging. The foldable smartphone combines its distinctive design with a fast-charging system and wireless charging support, offering users additional convenience when powering their devices. Google Pixel 9 Pro XL – Up to 37W Google’s Pixel 9 Pro XL supports fast wired charging using a compatible 45W USB-C charger. The device can reach approximately 70 per cent battery capacity

item.title: Houthi rebels close in on Aden, Yemeni forces dig in behind fortified line
item.description: Iran-backed Houthi rebels have advanced to within about 60 kilometers of the seat of Yemen’s internationally recognized government in the southern city of Aden, but the forces fighting them have set up a fortified line to defend the city, a military official said Tuesday. The Houthis' advance toward Aden has come after forces allied with the government withdrew from areas on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, allowing the Houthis to consolidate their grip on territory around the crucial waterway.

item.title: Exiled Catalan separatist Puigdemont to return to Spain after election
item.description: Catalan separatist ​and former regional leader Carles Puigdemont said on Wednesday he would end nearly a decade of self-imposed exile in Belgium and return to Spain on December 12, ​after ‌this weekend's national election. Puigdemont, whose legal troubles in ⁠Spain are over after the Supreme Court earlier this week applied an amnesty law to shelve the ‌criminal case against him, said at a televised news conference from ⁠Brussels that he would unveil his proposal for a renewed Catalan independence push on December 17. FRANCE 24's Sarah Morris reports from Madrid, Spain.

item.title: Premier League’s burst of early sendings-off may not last – but red cards are on the rise for a reason
item.description: While referees tend to reach for red early in the season before easing off, players are under increasing pressure to keep pace in a frenetic environment Off! Off! Off! The past three Premier League games have featured a red card, each for a different reason. Brighton’s Costinha was sent off for two bookings at Hull , Leny Yoro collected a red card against Liverpool for denying a goalscoring opportunity ( though his suspension was overturned on appeal ) and James Tarkowski saw red for serious foul play at Brentford . This season is shaping up to be an outlier in the VAR era of officiating in English football. The latest red cards took the Premier League total to 22 in 2026-27. The rate of 0.2 per game equates to 76 across the whole season, which would equal the Premier League record set in 2005-06. Refereeing has evolved in the past decade, though. The average across the seven completed campaigns since VAR was introduced is 0.12 per game, with a high of 0.15 in 2023-24. Continue reading...

The past three Premier League games have featured a red card, each for a different reason. Brighton’s Costinha was sent off for two bookings at Hull , Leny Yoro collected a red card against Liverpool for denying a goalscoring opportunity ( though his suspension was overturned on appeal ) and James Tarkowski saw red for serious foul play at Brentford . This season is shaping up to be an outlier in the VAR era of officiating in English football. The latest red cards took the Premier League total to 22 in 2026-27. The rate of 0.2 per game equates to 76 across the whole season, which would equal the Premier League record set in 2005-06. Refereeing has evolved in the past decade, though. The average across the seven completed campaigns since VAR was introduced is 0.12 per game, with a high of 0.15 in 2023-24. Continue reading...

item.title: Microsoft fixes Office dialog that had nothing to say and wouldn't go away
item.description: Microsoft has released a fix for a baffling bug that threw a blank window over Office applications and brought work to a standstill. The problem appeared when users launched an affected Office app, which could display an empty dialog box with no text and no buttons. Because the dialog offered no way to close it, some users were locked out of their work entirely, unable to continue until the issue was resolved. The good news is that there's an update to fix the problem – version 2611, build 16.0.20625.20142. The bad news is that you might not be able to launch the applications to perform the update because of that blank dialog window. Microsoft instructs affected users to save their work, close all Office applications, and open Command Prompt as administrator. They can then force the update with: "%programfiles%\Common Files\Microsoft Shared\ClickToRun\officec2rclient.exe" /update user updatetoversion=16.0.20625.20142 The glitch affects a swathe of Microsoft 365 products – Excel, Word, Outlook, PowerPoint, Access, and OneNote. Users reported the problem on Microsoft's forums , where volunteer moderator Stefan Blom noted that "this seems to be a common error at the moment" and suggested users try an Office repair or the more thorough Online Repair. Online Repair reinstalls Office, however, some users reported activation and sign-in problems alongside the blank windows, which may hint at the cause. Microsoft has yet to elucidate. Other users found that rolling back Office resolved the issue, while several reported that signing in with another application, such as Edge, fixed things. For administrators preparing fleets of devices, a dialog that blocks first use creates another deployment headache. One user with E3 licensing reported: "We can't just hand off a staged machine without getting call[s] that our new users can't get Office to work because of the blank licensing window." Microsoft has shared a fix for the problem, but has not stated which versions of its productivity applications were affected, nor has it explained what went wrong. The fix is welcome. An explanation of how Office ended up blocking users with a window containing nothing at all would be welcome too. ®

item.title: 2027: Tinubu has fulfilled promise made to Igbo after civil war – Kalu
item.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe, Umuahia Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Hon. Benjamin Kalu, has said that President Bola Tinubu has fulfilled the promise made to the Igbo after the civil war in 1970. He noted that at the end of the civil war, the federal government had announced the policy of Reconciliation, Reconstruction and Rehabilitation to rebuild Igbo land, alleging that successive administrations failed to implement the policy. The Deputy Speaker stated that Tinubu is the only president that has made meaningful efforts in implementing the policy by establishing the South East Development Commission (SEDC) and putting up infrastructural projects and political appointments across the South East zone. Kalu, who stated this in Umuahia during the donation of 25 vehicles to the Abia State chapter of the Door to Door mobilisation by High Chief Government Ekpemupolo, urged the Igbo to re-elect the president to finish his job in the next four years. “For over 50 years, nobody was able to fulfil the promise made to the Igbo after the civil war. Gone are the days of promise. Today, President Bola Tinubu has fulfilled the promise he has given the South East Development Commission (SEDC). He has also given the SEDC the permission to open what is known as the South East Investment Company. And he has funded the company with billions of Naira. “Today, the company has started the project of piping gas across the Southeast. The companies in Lagos and Kano will start coming to build in the Southeast. This is the president that Tompolo wants us to support. “Across the South East, more roads are springing up because our son is the Minister of Works, Engr Dave Umahi. I can’t remember the last time an Igbo man was the Minister of Works. Umahi has been making us proud. The President also appointed Ojukwu as the Minister of Foreign Affairs and another Igbo as the Chief of Naval Staff. The Minister of State for Finance is also an Igbo. “The President has also invested money in securing our lives and properties. The Ministry of Defence budget has increased; employment in the military and police is increasing. The president has also supported state police. Salaries are not being owed because Tinubu removed the fuel subsidy and released more money for the sub-nations. He urged the Igbo to reject anyone who is campaigning for the South East zone to serve for only a four-year term, stressing that when the time comes, the zone would take eight years, as others have done. “Reject them when they come to you that they have signed an agreement for the Igbo to serve for only four years. The Igbo will not wait after 60 years to receive power for only four years. We didn’t wait for 60 years for the Igbo to take only half the bread. Other zones have done right years; when the time comes, the Igbo will take eight years, not four years.” The post 2027: Tinubu has fulfilled promise made to Igbo after civil war – Kalu appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Meet Jessi Kalambayi: Miss Universe DRC Who Made the Top 12 at Miss Universe 2026
item.description: Miss Universe Congo Jessi Kalambayi wearing her national crown and sash in a gold beaded evening gown. Photo Credit: Jessi Kalambayi/Instagram The 75th Miss Universe competition has come to a close in San Juan, Puerto Rico, and Jessi Kalambayi gave the Democratic Republic of the Congo a night to remember. Out of 116 contestants from around the world—and 17 representing Africa —the 28-year-old beauty queen became the sole African delegate to reach the Top 12 at Tuesday night’s live finale, representing her country as Miss Universe Congo at the Coliseo de Puerto Rico José Miguel Agrelot. That is a major result for the Central African nation, and there is quite a story behind the woman who made it happen. Born Jessi Longwe Kalambayi in Kinshasa and raised between South Africa and the United States, Jessi arrived at Miss Universe with an impressive background beyond pageantry. She holds a bachelor’s degree in Psychology with a minor in Africana Studies from Metropolitan State University of Denver, as well as a master’s degree in International Studies, specialising in Migration, from the University of Denver. Her professional experience includes working as a programme manager supporting refugee resettlement. She has also used her platform to speak about embracing natural African hair textures, from afros to braids, as part of celebrating Congolese identity. Miss Universe Congo Jessi Kalambayi honours the Democratic Republic of the Congo national football team for her Miss Universe 2026 national costume. Photo Credit: Jessi Kalambayi/Instagram And this was hardly her first time navigating a major pageant stage. Before winning the Miss Universe DRC 2026 crown in July, succeeding Dorcas Dienda, Jessi had already made her mark in the United States. In 2024, she won Miss Colorado USA and went on to place in the Top 10 at Miss USA. That experience came in handy in San Juan, where she moved through the preliminary rounds and closed-door interviews with the nine-member selection committee to secure a place in the initial Top 30. Miss Universe Congo Jessi Kalambayi on stage during the swimsuit round of the Miss Universe 2026 Preliminary Competition. Photo Credit: Jessi Kalambayi/Instagram Finale night brought another big moment. Alongside fellow African Top 30 semifinalists from Ethiopia, Guinea, Tanzania and Uganda, Jessi made it through the swimsuit round and advanced into the Top 12 alongside contestants from Puerto Rico, Venezuela, the Philippines, the United States and France—standing as Africa’s lone representative in that round. Miss Universe Congo Jessi Kalambayi during the Top 12 evening gown round at the 75th Miss Universe finale in San Juan, Puerto Rico. Photo Credit: Jessi Kalambayi/Instagram Her Miss Universe journey came to an end just before the announcement of the Top 5, while Puerto Rico’s Jennifer Barreto went on to claim the crown. Still, Jessi’s run marked an important showing for the Democratic Republic of the Congo and closed out the 75th

item.title: Osubi Airport simulates air crash after 20 years
item.description: …Drill identifies emergency response gaps, need for modern equipment By Egufe Yafugborhi WARRI — The Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN), Alfred Diete-Spiff Airport, Osubi, Delta State, has conducted its first simulated aircraft crash rescue exercise in about 20 years to assess its emergency response capabilities and identify areas requiring improvement. The exercise, conducted at about 1:30pm on the airport’s airside, simulated an aircraft crash involving passengers who sustained varying degrees of injuries. Several emergency response agencies participated in the drill, including the Nigerian Navy Hospital and Air Station Fire Service, Nigeria Police Force, Delta State Fire Service, Nigerian Red Cross Society, Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB), Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, Delta Procare Hospital, Nigerian Ports Authority Health Service and Renaissance Africa Energy Fire Service. Speaking after the exercise, the Airport Manager, Winston Egwuatu, expressed satisfaction with the outcome, saying identified operational gaps would be addressed to strengthen the airport’s emergency response capacity. He explained that the exercise was designed to test the preparedness of personnel, availability of equipment and effectiveness of established emergency procedures. “No simulation exercise is perfect. It was actually meant to test the preparedness of both the officers who are going to be deployed, the materials and also the procedures. “The purpose of this is to identify the gaps and close them, so that when it is deployed, we will deploy better,” he said. Egwuatu, who spoke alongside departmental heads, said observers from the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA) identified areas requiring improvement, particularly personnel training and retraining. He noted that the airport had recorded operational improvements since its transition from an airstrip but stressed the need for additional operational vehicles and modern firefighting equipment. “Within resources available to the management of the airport, we have done very well. This airport used to be an airstrip. Now it’s operating as an airport. That means there have been some level of upgrade. “However, there is need for improvement in regards to operational vehicles and state-of-the-art fire tankers to meet the time that we find ourselves now,” he said. The airport manager disclosed that observations from the exercise would be compiled into a comprehensive report to guide corrective measures and requests requiring intervention from higher authorities. He also emphasised the importance of effective collaboration among emergency response agencies, noting that prompt intervention could determine survival during an aircraft accident. “It is in the interest of everybody to deploy, all of us who have the wherewithal to not just respond, but respond timely. Because that timely response is critical. It can save the life of someone,” Egwuatu said. He commended the participating

He explained that the exercise was designed to test the preparedness of personnel, availability of equipment and effectiveness of established emergency procedures. “No simulation exercise is perfect. It was actually meant to test the preparedness of both the officers who are going to be deployed, the materials and also the procedures. “The purpose of this is to identify the gaps and close them, so that when it is deployed, we will deploy better,” he said. Egwuatu, who spoke alongside departmental heads, said observers from the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA) identified areas requiring improvement, particularly personnel training and retraining. He noted that the airport had recorded operational improvements since its transition from an airstrip but stressed the need for additional operational vehicles and modern firefighting equipment. “Within resources available to the management of the airport, we have done very well. This airport used to be an airstrip. Now it’s operating as an airport. That means there have been some level of upgrade. “However, there is need for improvement in regards to operational vehicles and state-of-the-art fire tankers to meet the time that we find ourselves now,” he said. The airport manager disclosed that observations from the exercise would be compiled into a comprehensive report to guide corrective measures and requests requiring intervention from higher authorities. He also emphasised the importance of effective collaboration among emergency response agencies, noting that prompt intervention could determine survival during an aircraft accident. “It is in the interest of everybody to deploy, all of us who have the wherewithal to not just respond, but respond timely. Because that timely response is critical. It can save the life of someone,” Egwuatu said. He commended the participating organisations and other stakeholders for their cooperation, adding that FAAN planned to produce a video documentary of the exercise for educational purposes and to promote improved emergency preparedness. Earlier, NCAA observers, Maureen Amewhule and Engr. Okrinade Ahmed, commended the airport management for organising the simulation, praising the alertness, professionalism and coordination demonstrated by personnel during the exercise. They, however, called for more training, particularly for medical personnel, improved inter-agency collaboration and regular engagements among stakeholders. The exercise, which is a regulatory requirement of the NCAA, was conducted without disrupting normal airport operations. item.title: Trump announces new tariffs on EU, China despite US midterms defeat
item.description: President Donald Trump's administration on Wednesday reignited global trade tensions by proposing new tariffs on some of the largest US trading partners, including the EU, Japan and Taiwan. China could be slapped with a 20 percent tariff, a senior official said. The announcement came weeks after a cost-of-living crisis landed the Republicans a sweeping defeat in the US midterms.

item.title: ‘Incoming President’, Titi celebrates Atiku, says ex-VP not tired at 80
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Wife of the former Vice President, Atiku Abubakar, has described her husband as the “incoming President of Nigeria” as he turned 80 on Wednesday, saying he is “not tired” and that his vision for the country is “even clearer.” In a birthday tribute titled “Daddy at 80”, Chief Amina Titi Atiku Abubakar, the former Second Lady of Nigeria, said she was celebrating “the Incoming President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria come May 29th, 2027 by the Special Grace of God.” “At 80, you are not tired. At 80, your vision for Nigeria is even clearer. I have walked with you through valleys and mountains, and I know what God has placed in you for Nigeria,” she wrote. She said Nigeria needed his “experience,” his “capacity, and your compassionate heart now more than ever.” According to her, this is “reflecting in the enthusiastic and passionate ways Nigerians turned out to cheer you to victory as you articulate your policies and canvass support for your presidential aspiration come January 16, 2027.” Titi said the milestone coincided with 57 years of marriage. “Eighty years of a life well-lived and Fifty-seven years of a love that has stood the test of time. When I first met you as a young lady, I saw a cute, handsome, principled, brilliant, focused Customs officer with big dreams. I did not know I was meeting a destiny.” She credited her husband with the support that led her into the campaign against human trafficking. “Many men would have stopped their wife from confronting human trafficking. You did not. You not only gave me the wings to fly, but the inspiration, the courage, the confidence and the wherewithal to fight for humanity and the vulnerables. You told me, ‘Titi, go and save those girls.'” She said the Women Trafficking and Child Labour Eradication Foundation (WOTCLEF) was born from that encouragement in 1999. “A law was made to criminalize human trafficking in Nigeria and NAPTIP was established to save millions. “The woman I am today – the Lecturer, the Advocate, the Amazing Amazon, the Former Second Lady of Nigeria, the Grand Matron to several Organizations – I am because you allowed me to become,” she said. Titi also paid tribute to Atiku’s record in public service. “Nigeria has known you as a diligent Customs Officer, a successful businessman, a two-term Vice President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria who chaired the National Economic Council that paid off the country’s foreign debt and a democrat who has kept faith with democracy even when it was costly. You don’t just make promises; you build systems. You don’t just talk about privatization and jobs; you did it. “Only few people know how many school fees you pay silently; how many widows you feed daily; how many young people you gave jobs in and out of government, how many lives you have touched directly or indirectly and how many destinies you have transformed positively. item.title: A familiar Iranian hacking group has found a new way to cause chaos
item.description: One night in October, hackers staged one of the most unusual cyber attacks in history : cranking up the temperature in refrigeration systems at hundreds of supermarkets across France and destroying millions of euros of food. Hackers have targeted commercial fridges and freezers before, but never at this scale and never in the heart of Europe. The brazen attack left cyber professionals unsure as to who might have executed such a madcap operation. But French intelligence agencies found traces of Farsi and other clues in the digital trail pointing to an elite hacking unit of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. The unit allegedly behind the hack, Shahid Kaveh, was already well known to Western intelligence agencies. Named after Mahmoud Kaveh, an Iranian commander who died during the 1980s Iran-Iraq war, it is one of several hacking units overseen by the Revolutionary Guards’ Cyber Electronic Command. Read full article Comments

item.title: Amazon is reportedly in talks to end Muse AI shopping block
item.description: Amazon has held talks about letting Meta's Muse AI agent shop on its online marketplace, according to a report from Fortune . The discussions, which could end Amazon's block on Muse , reportedly center on the kinds of products the AI agent recommends and the potential impact on the ecommerce giant's advertising revenue. As reported by Fortune , Amazon is concerned that it could lose advertising revenue by allowing Muse on its site, since it depends on actual humans seeing ads across its online marketplace. It's also reportedly worried about the quality of the product search results that Muse will present to users, as well as whether the AI age … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: Atiku embraces ‘Daddy Subsidy’ nickname, promises Nigerians relief at 80
item.description: Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has embraced the nickname “Daddy Subsidy” as he marked his 80th birthday on Wednesday, promising Nigerians that relief would come and pledging to make the country affordable again. Atiku, the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, made the remark in a post on X while thanking Nigerians for their birthday wishes and prayers. He said the nickname was among the names Nigerians had given him that he particularly enjoyed, adding that he remained committed to making life easier for citizens. Of all the names Nigerians have given me, "Daddy Subsidy" may be the one I enjoy most on my birthday. Thank you for your kind wishes, and for the prayer that warmed my afternoon. To the sons and daughters scattered across the country: relief is coming, and it will follow the… https://t.co/LZo7x3Mgf9 — Atiku Abubakar (@atiku) November 25, 2026 “Of all the names Nigerians have given me, ‘Daddy Subsidy’ may be the one I enjoy most on my birthday. Thank you for your kind wishes, and for the prayer that warmed my afternoon,” he wrote. Addressing Nigerians across the country, the former vice-president promised that relief was coming, making an apparent reference to his position on petrol subsidy and the hardship associated with its removal. “To the sons and daughters scattered across the country: relief is coming, and it will follow the barrel. I will make Nigeria affordable again,” Atiku added. Atiku’s birthday message comes amid continued political debate over the Tinubu administration’s economic reforms, particularly the removal of petrol subsidy, which has contributed to increased living and transportation costs. Meanwhile, President Bola Tinubu has congratulated Atiku on his 80th birthday, commending his contributions to Nigeria’s political development, democracy, education and the private sector. In a statement issued by his spokesman, Bayo Onanuga, Tinubu said he shared with Atiku a commitment to democratic pluralism, political participation and allowing Nigerians to present alternative ideas on governance. The president recalled supporting Atiku’s 2007 presidential ambition under the defunct Action Congress platform, saying the decision reflected his belief that democracy thrives when political actors are free to compete and contribute to national discourse. Tinubu also praised Atiku’s investments in education and entrepreneurship, particularly the establishment of the American University of Nigeria, Yola, which he said had contributed to expanding access to higher education and developing human capital. Despite their differences in political affiliation and views on national issues, Tinubu said their shared commitment to Nigeria’s unity and democratic stability remained important. He wished the former vice-president good health, renewed strength and many more years of service to Nigeria and humanity as he joined the octogenarian club. item.title: JetBrains finds agents may cheat with open source
item.description: JetBrains has revamped a benchmark for evaluating large language models after suspecting too many agents gamed their tasks the first time round. The company labelled this agentic practice "reward hacking" in a post summarizing the results of its revised evaluation. Like its predecessor , Kotlin Benchmark 2.0 is a collection of tasks that evaluates how well AI coding agents work with the Kotlin programming language , in order to help Kotlin programmers decide which agent-model configurations to use. The tasks include fixing tricky problems in Kotlin code across different domains, and making corrections to multiple files. Dirty data The revised benchmar k now includes 30 Kotlin multi-file code problems that have not been exposed to the public in any way before. The revised test all but guarantees that the agents have not encountered this set of problems, or potential solutions, before. Another 70 tasks are based on code that resides in public repositories. The test also blocked all network access for the open source tasks, except for what was needed to communicate with the model itself. This minimized the possibility that the agent could look for an existing answer already posted, perhaps through a patch or pull request. A 30-minute limit was set for each task. Overall, the agents were significantly less accurate when solving problems on codebases they had never encountered. Top resolution rates dropped rather suspiciously from 86.2 percent on tasks based on open source repositories to 60 percent on those based on closed source repositories. Although the agents lacked network access, JetBrains boffins theorized that they might have benefited from encountering and internalizing these open source repositories during training. Only the private repositories were completely new to them. Also curious was how a different set of models excelled at the closed source problems, compared to those models that usually did better on the open source tasks. Leaderboard Shakeup When restricted to closed source tasks, two dark horse models rose to the top: Gemini 3.8 Flash, via Antigravity CLI, topped the list with a 60 percent success rate, closely followed by DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (running on OpenCode) at 58.9 percent. Of the two, the open weight DeepSeek was far cheaper (at $0.08 per task) than the closed weight Gemini ($1.74 per task), however. In contrast, Opus 5.5 completed only 53.3 percent of the tasks at $1.21 per task, and Fable 5.1 completed only 44.4 percent of the tasks, at a luxurious $3.27 per task. Claude Code harnessed both of these models. Claude’s lackluster completion rates on closed source tasks are somewhat sus given how both of these Anthropic models scored significantly higher on tasks using open source materials. In fact Claude ran the table when it came to open source: Fable 5.1 topped the charts with 86.2 percent accuracy, closely followed by Opus 5.5 at 84.8 percent accuracy. item.dc:creator: Joab Jackson
item.content:encoded: JetBrains has revamped a benchmark for evaluating large language models after suspecting too many agents gamed their tasks the first time round. The company labelled this agentic practice "reward hacking" in a post summarizing the results of its revised evaluation. Like its predecessor , Kotlin Benchmark 2.0 is a collection of tasks that evaluates how well AI coding agents work with the Kotlin programming language , in order to help Kotlin programmers decide which agent-model configurations to use. The tasks include fixing tricky problems in Kotlin code across different domains, and making corrections to multiple files. Dirty data The revised benchmar k now includes 30 Kotlin multi-file code problems that have not been exposed to the public in any way before. The revised test all but guarantees that the agents have not encountered this set of problems, or potential solutions, before. Another 70 tasks are based on code that resides in public repositories. The test also blocked all network access for the open source tasks, except for what was needed to communicate with the model itself. This minimized the possibility that the agent could look for an existing answer already posted, perhaps through a patch or pull request. A 30-minute limit was set for each task. Overall, the agents were significantly less accurate when solving problems on codebases they had never encountered. Top resolution rates dropped rather suspiciously from 86.2 percent on tasks based on open source repositories to 60 percent on those based on closed source repositories. Although the agents lacked network access, JetBrains boffins theorized that they might have benefited from encountering and internalizing these open source repositories during training. Only the private repositories were completely new to them. Also curious was how a different set of models excelled at the closed source problems, compared to those models that usually did better on the open source tasks. Leaderboard Shakeup When restricted to closed source tasks, two dark horse models rose to the top: Gemini 3.8 Flash, via Antigravity CLI, topped the list with a 60 percent success rate, closely followed by DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (running on OpenCode) at 58.9 percent. Of the two, the open weight DeepSeek was far cheaper (at $0.08 per task) than the closed weight Gemini ($1.74 per task), however. In contrast, Opus 5.5 completed only 53.3 percent of the tasks at $1.21 per task, and Fable 5.1 completed only 44.4 percent of the tasks, at a luxurious $3.27 per task. Claude Code harnessed both of these models. Claude’s lackluster completion rates on closed source tasks are somewhat sus given how both of these Anthropic models scored significantly higher on tasks using open source materials. In fact Claude ran the table when it came to open source: Fable 5.1 topped the charts with 86.2 percent accuracy, closely followed by Opus 5.5 at 84.8 percent accuracy. (Kotlin users will pay dearly for the extra sliver of Anthropic accuracy: The average cost of Fable completing a Kotlin cleanup task runs $2.38, while Opus could do the job for $0.68.) Gaming the boss One possible interpretation of these disparate numbers is that models are drawing from their own knowledge bases instead of reasoning from scratch. Whether this is cheating or the models simply working as intended might be more a matter of philosophical debate. Mark Hinkle, founder of the AIE Network consultancy, suspects the issue of integrity may go deeper. "Private code doesn't stop reward hacking, it changes the shortcut," he wrote to The Register on LinkedIn. "On public code the agent goes and finds the answer somebody has already published. On private code there's no answer to find, so it satisfies whatever is checking it. I treat these things like entry-level employees, and a sharp new hire figures out fast what the boss actually looks at." JetBrains did not immediately respond to a request for comment, but concluded in its post that more investigation is needed. It promises that its people will pore over the open source results to see if any have been contaminated by the LLMs' own memory. It also plans to run its own static analysis tool, Qodana , against the results to check for errors. Sireesha Pulipati , a staff data engineer and AI observer, suggested, also by LinkedIn, that JetBrains may have needed more specificity in its agent instructions. "Out of the box [an agent] tends to reach for generic patterns. But when we give it instructions and skills that tell it where to look for our patterns and context, it follows them. A well-controlled harness, with those standards built in, is what makes the agent useful," Pulipati wrote. So good on JetBrains for providing Kotlin users some information about working with AI, but, as always, AI benchmarks should be approached with extreme side-eye. ®

item.title: 'Historic' space mission: China launches Shenzhou 24 spacecraft carrying Pakistani astronaut
item.description: China on Wednesday launched the Shenzhou 24 spacecraft with three astronauts — two Chinese and a Pakistani — sending the first foreign crew member to its space station. It successfully separated from a rocket and entered its predetermined orbit. The launch marked the first joint flight involving Chinese and foreign astronauts in the history of China’s crewed space program.

Four millionaires every day and one ₦10 million weekly jackpot winner every Sunday, announced live by 8 pm on Pepsi ‘s Instagram page, @pepsi_naija. Seven-Up Bottling Company’s (SBC) Pepsi Agba Baller Promo is giving consumers across selected regions the opportunity to win cash rewards simply by purchasing participating products and entering their unique codes. Running from November 2, 2026, to January 3, 2027, the promotion is open to eligible consumers in nine participating regions: Lagos, Ogun, Oyo, Kwara, Osun, Ekiti, Kogi, Niger and Ondo. If you have been wondering how to participate, which products qualify or what happens when you win, here’s everything you need to know about the Pepsi Agba Baller Promo. What Is the Pepsi Agba Baller Promo? The Pepsi Agba Baller Promo is a consumer rewards initiative by Seven-Up Bottling Company, featuring Pepsi and other participating Seven-Up Bottling Company products with a yellow cover. The campaign gives consumers the chance to win exciting cash prizes by purchasing eligible products with the yellow promotional covers and entering the unique codes underneath. What’s Up For Grabs? The ₦800 million prize pool offers several opportunities to win throughout the campaign: Win Every Minute: One winner emerges every minute between 8 a.m. and 8 p.m. daily. Daily Millionaires: Four winners receive ₦1 million each every day. Weekly Mega Jackpot: One participant wins ₦10 million in the weekly mega jackpot every Sunday. Who Can Participate? To be eligible for the promo and receive prizes won, participants must: Be at least 18 years old. Reside in one of the nine participating states. Have a valid National Identification Number (NIN) or Bank Verification Number (BVN). Use a mobile number registered in their own name with NIMC. Have a personal bank account registered in their own name for prize payments. How to Participate in the Pepsi Agba Baller Promo To participate, look out for plastic bottles of Pepsi, 7UP, Mirinda, Teem and other eligible Seven-Up Bottling Company products carrying the distinctive yellow promotional cover, then follow these steps: Step 1: Buy a Participating Product Purchase an eligible product with the distinctive yellow promotional cover. Step 2: Retrieve Your Code Open the bottle and check underneath the cover for your unique promotional code. Step 3: Enter Your Code Dial *7022# on your mobile phone and follow the prompts, or scan the QR code on the bottle or promotional materials to enter. The promotion covers participating Seven-Up Bottling Company products carrying the yellow promotional cover, including Pepsi, 7UP, Mirinda and Teem. item.title: ‘Despite our differences, Nigeria comes first’ – Tinubu celebrates Atiku at 80
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab President Bola Tinubu has congratulated former Vice President Atiku Abubakar on his 80th birthday, noting that despite their political differences and occasional disagreements, their shared commitment to Nigeria’s unity and democratic stability must remain paramount. Tinubu, in a birthday message issued on Wednesday, November 25, 2026, commended Atiku’s contributions to Nigeria’s development, particularly his years of political engagement and commitment to democratic pluralism. The message was shared by the President’s Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga. Tinubu recalled that he supported Atiku’s 2007 presidential ambition, saying the decision reflected his belief that democracy thrives when political actors are free to participate, offer alternative visions and contribute to discussions on leadership and governance. He said his political philosophy had consistently emphasised strengthening democratic institutions, respecting divergent opinions and ensuring that political competition served the interests of Nigerians. The President also reiterated his advocacy for politics without bitterness, saying room should always be left for reconciliation after disagreements among political opponents. “Despite our different political affiliations and occasional disagreements, Nigeria’s democracy must continue to benefit from citizens who remain committed to democratic engagement, national development, and the rule of law,” he said. Tinubu also commended Atiku’s contributions to education, entrepreneurship and the private sector, particularly his establishment of the American University of Nigeria, Yola, which he said had expanded access to quality higher education and strengthened human capital development. Although he acknowledged that he and Atiku now belonged to different political camps and held contrasting views on national issues, Tinubu said their shared commitment to Nigeria’s unity and democratic stability should remain paramount. “Therefore, as the former vice president joins the Octogenarian Club, I wish him good health, renewed strength and many more years of service to the nation and humanity,” he said. “Happy 80th birthday, Your Excellency,” the President added. Atiku, who served as Nigeria’s vice president from 1999 to 2007, has contested the presidency several times and is the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate for the 2027 elections. The post ‘Despite our differences, Nigeria comes first’ – Tinubu celebrates Atiku at 80 appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.content:encoded: By Enitan Abdultawab President Bola Tinubu has congratulated former Vice President Atiku Abubakar on his 80th birthday, noting that despite their political differences and occasional disagreements, their shared commitment to Nigeria’s unity and democratic stability must remain paramount. Tinubu, in a birthday message issued on Wednesday, November 25, 2026, commended Atiku’s contributions to Nigeria’s development, particularly his years of political engagement and commitment to democratic pluralism. The message was shared by the President’s Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga. Tinubu recalled that he supported Atiku’s 2007 presidential ambition, saying the decision reflected his belief that democracy thrives when political actors are free to participate, offer alternative visions and contribute to discussions on leadership and governance. He said his political philosophy had consistently emphasised strengthening democratic institutions, respecting divergent opinions and ensuring that political competition served the interests of Nigerians. The President also reiterated his advocacy for politics without bitterness, saying room should always be left for reconciliation after disagreements among political opponents. “Despite our different political affiliations and occasional disagreements, Nigeria’s democracy must continue to benefit from citizens who remain committed to democratic engagement, national development, and the rule of law,” he said. Tinubu also commended Atiku’s contributions to education, entrepreneurship and the private sector, particularly his establishment of the American University of Nigeria, Yola, which he said had expanded access to quality higher education and strengthened human capital development. Although he acknowledged that he and Atiku now belonged to different political camps and held contrasting views on national issues, Tinubu said their shared commitment to Nigeria’s unity and democratic stability should remain paramount. “Therefore, as the former vice president joins the Octogenarian Club, I wish him good health, renewed strength and many more years of service to the nation and humanity,” he said. “Happy 80th birthday, Your Excellency,” the President added. Atiku, who served as Nigeria’s vice president from 1999 to 2007, has contested the presidency several times and is the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate for the 2027 elections. The post ‘Despite our differences, Nigeria comes first’ – Tinubu celebrates Atiku at 80 appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Reps order contractor back to failed East-west road culverts
item.description: …Demand urgent repairs, four-week monitoring of project By Gift Chapi-Odekina, Abuja ABUJA — The House of Representatives has urged the Federal Ministry of Works to direct Rock Result Nigeria Limited to return immediately to the site and rehabilitate or reconstruct damaged box culverts along the East-West Road, particularly at Iheke in Ahoada East Local Government Area of Rivers State. The resolution followed the adoption of a motion sponsored by Hon. Oboku Abonsizibe Oforji, who drew the attention of lawmakers to the reported deterioration of the culverts and the need for urgent intervention to prevent further damage and potential safety risks. The House recalled that it had, on October 3, 2023, adopted a motion on the deplorable condition of the East-West Road, particularly the Iheke axis, following which the Federal Government undertook further interventions. The interventions included the construction of box culverts, approval and release of funds for rehabilitation and flood mitigation works, payments to Rock Result Nigeria Limited and the re-award of the contract to Setraco Nigeria Limited for the continuation of the road dualisation project. However, lawmakers expressed concern over reports that the constructed box culverts had deteriorated, despite the financial commitments made by the government. They said the reported condition of the drainage infrastructure underscored the need for a technical assessment of the works, including the materials used, construction standards and supervision of the project. The House noted that the East-West Road was a major economic and social corridor connecting Bayelsa, Rivers and Delta states to other parts of the country, serving communities and facilitating the movement of people, goods and services. It warned that the deteriorating condition of the road could further disrupt transportation and expose motorists and other road users to safety risks. Lawmakers also expressed concern that the dualisation of the East-West Road from Ahoada in Rivers State through the Bayelsa axis to Patani in Delta State remained incomplete, despite earlier completion targets of April 2025 and November 2025. Consequently, the House urged the Ministry of Works to ensure that Rock Result Nigeria Limited returned to the site without delay to carry out the required rehabilitation or reconstruction of the damaged culverts in accordance with approved engineering standards. It also called for adequate technical supervision, quality assurance and an independent engineering assessment of the remedial works to reduce the risk of further structural problems. In addition, the lawmakers urged the ministry to ensure the completion of the dualisation of the Ahoada-Bayelsa and Patani sections of the road by Setraco Nigeria Limited. The House mandated its Committee on Works and Legislative Compliance to monitor the implementation of the resolutions and report back within four weeks for further legislative action. item.title: YABATECH non-teaching staff threaten indefinite strike
item.description: …Protest over unpaid allowances, give management until Thursday By Adesina Wahab Non-teaching staff of Yaba College of Technology (YABATECH), Lagos, on Wednesday protested the non-payment of several allowances owed them, threatening to embark on an indefinite strike from Thursday if their demands were not met. The workers, under the umbrella of the Non-Teaching Staff Union of Polytechnics (NOTSUP), staged a protest march around the campus, led by the union’s Branch Chairman, Bayo Sanusi. They marched to the Administrative Block, which houses the Rector’s office, the Bursary Department and the institution’s main gate, singing solidarity songs and displaying placards bearing various messages. Addressing the protesters, Sanusi expressed displeasure over what he described as the exclusion of non-teaching staff from the payment of allowances, despite the reported payment of similar entitlements to teaching staff. He said teaching and non-teaching employees played complementary roles in the administration of tertiary institutions and should be treated fairly. “I don’t know whether our people have seen a bird flying with one wing. It is not possible. Tertiary institutions like ours have teaching and non-teaching staff and we complement one another. NOTSUP is made up of NASU and SSANIP members and we are united in calling for the payment of our dues. A labourer, they say, is worth his wages,” he said. Sanusi said the union’s national leadership had engaged the Federal Government on the outstanding allowances and reached an agreement on their payment. He added that the Minister of Education had directed the managements of federal polytechnics and colleges of education to source funds for the payments from available resources, including savings from capital expenditure and internally generated revenue, with a promise that the Federal Government would reimburse the institutions. According to him, at least three federal polytechnics had complied with the directive and paid the allowances, while non-teaching staff at YABATECH were still awaiting payment. He said the union had engaged the college management and was assured last Wednesday that the outstanding entitlements would be paid, but the promise had yet to be fulfilled. “In line with the directive by the Minister, at least three federal Polytechnics have paid. item.dc:creator: Nwafor
item.content:encoded: …Protest over unpaid allowances, give management until Thursday By Adesina Wahab Non-teaching staff of Yaba College of Technology (YABATECH), Lagos, on Wednesday protested the non-payment of several allowances owed them, threatening to embark on an indefinite strike from Thursday if their demands were not met. The workers, under the umbrella of the Non-Teaching Staff Union of Polytechnics (NOTSUP), staged a protest march around the campus, led by the union’s Branch Chairman, Bayo Sanusi. They marched to the Administrative Block, which houses the Rector’s office, the Bursary Department and the institution’s main gate, singing solidarity songs and displaying placards bearing various messages. Addressing the protesters, Sanusi expressed displeasure over what he described as the exclusion of non-teaching staff from the payment of allowances, despite the reported payment of similar entitlements to teaching staff. He said teaching and non-teaching employees played complementary roles in the administration of tertiary institutions and should be treated fairly. “I don’t know whether our people have seen a bird flying with one wing. It is not possible. Tertiary institutions like ours have teaching and non-teaching staff and we complement one another. NOTSUP is made up of NASU and SSANIP members and we are united in calling for the payment of our dues. A labourer, they say, is worth his wages,” he said. Sanusi said the union’s national leadership had engaged the Federal Government on the outstanding allowances and reached an agreement on their payment. He added that the Minister of Education had directed the managements of federal polytechnics and colleges of education to source funds for the payments from available resources, including savings from capital expenditure and internally generated revenue, with a promise that the Federal Government would reimburse the institutions. According to him, at least three federal polytechnics had complied with the directive and paid the allowances, while non-teaching staff at YABATECH were still awaiting payment. He said the union had engaged the college management and was assured last Wednesday that the outstanding entitlements would be paid, but the promise had yet to be fulfilled. “In line with the directive by the Minister, at least three federal Polytechnics have paid. Here at YABATECH, teaching staff have been paid leaving us in the lurch like orphans. We are not less human than teaching staff. We have contacted our management here and last Wednesday, they promised to pay. A week has passed and nothing has happened,” he said. The union chairman questioned why the management had been able to pay teaching staff but had yet to settle the entitlements of non-teaching employees. He said the rising cost of living had worsened the hardship faced by workers, citing the daily transport expenses incurred by some staff members who commute from areas such as Ikorodu to the college. Sanusi also expressed concern over the personal challenges confronting members, including difficulties in meeting healthcare and other living expenses. He clarified that the protest was not motivated by any personal disagreement with the Rector or Bursar, but was aimed at pressing the management to address the workers’ demands. The union leader also rejected suggestions that the outstanding allowances could be paid next year, after the elections, insisting that members could no longer wait. “We cannot take that. We cannot wait any longer as we have waited enough,” he said. On the union’s next line of action, Sanusi said its branch leadership would consult the national leadership and await further directives, warning that an indefinite strike could commence from Thursday. The demands include payment of 10 months’ arrears of the Consolidated Non-Teaching Tool Allowance (CONTTA), nine months’ Earned Allowance, 12 months’ arrears of the 25 and 35 per cent allowances, as well as outstanding promotion arrears. item.title: ‘Nobody showed up but me’: will Friendsgiving survive gen Z?
item.description: A generation known for loneliness is putting their own spin on a millennial-made tradition that requires socializing It’s a TikTok scene straight out of a stress dream: two men stand in their freshly cleaned apartment, explaining how all but one of the people they invited to Friendsgiving flaked out at the last minute. There is a can of whipped cream on the table and a 6lb ham in the oven. According to the video, posted by pop-culture podcaster Jackson Strike, those who ditched were either tired, or sick, or had a difficult day at work. More than 1.5 million people liked the video and many flooded to the comments section to express their disappointment at what they saw as an epidemic of antisocial behavior. “Everyone wants a village until they have to be a villager,” one user wrote. “Time to get new friends,” quipped another. Continue reading...

item.title: Hannah Fry: The bizarre reason humans are so vulnerable to choking
item.description: Fran Pulido One of the unexpectedly delightful things about becoming a well-known nerd is that other nerds, often with far more interesting jobs than mine, have started hunting me down in social settings to tell me the nerdiest things they know. It almost always ends up being totally fascinating, and only occasionally mildly traumatising. At a kid’s birthday party recently, I got chatting to one of the dads, who happens to be an ear, nose and throat consultant. I asked him if he used robotics for his surgeries. He said no, then proceeded to mime what he actually did instead. There followed a series of alarmingly enthusiastic slashing motions, like a scene from a horror movie, while in the background a group of 9-year-old girls sat quietly painting. Advertisement Free newsletter Sign up to Professor Hannah Fry’s column Sign up to newsletter But the most bizarre thing about that conversation wasn’t the surgeon’s graphic re-enactment, it was what he went on to say about the totally ridiculous, illogical design of the human throat and what it tells us about the path of evolution. The story starts by noticing that the human body (if you ignore all the unimportant bits hanging off the sides like limbs) is essentially just one giant tube. Topologically, this makes perfect sense. Back in the earliest days of animal life, some organisms tried a flat design, like a pancake, with digestion done on one side. Others tried a little pocket, with the same opening serving as entrance and exit. But the one-way tube proved to be the most successful, because it allowed our ancestors to process their last meal while eating their next. Those early creatures would travel through the world mouth first, which is why the sensory equipment evolved to be gathered around that end, with a brain nearby to make sense of everything. New research into its origins is amazing My lovely father died of Alzheimer’s last year, and since then, I’ve been digging into the disease to try to understand what happened to him. item.dc:creator: Hannah Fry
item.content:encoded: Fran Pulido One of the unexpectedly delightful things about becoming a well-known nerd is that other nerds, often with far more interesting jobs than mine, have started hunting me down in social settings to tell me the nerdiest things they know. It almost always ends up being totally fascinating, and only occasionally mildly traumatising. At a kid’s birthday party recently, I got chatting to one of the dads, who happens to be an ear, nose and throat consultant. I asked him if he used robotics for his surgeries. He said no, then proceeded to mime what he actually did instead. There followed a series of alarmingly enthusiastic slashing motions, like a scene from a horror movie, while in the background a group of 9-year-old girls sat quietly painting. Advertisement Free newsletter Sign up to Professor Hannah Fry’s column Sign up to newsletter But the most bizarre thing about that conversation wasn’t the surgeon’s graphic re-enactment, it was what he went on to say about the totally ridiculous, illogical design of the human throat and what it tells us about the path of evolution. The story starts by noticing that the human body (if you ignore all the unimportant bits hanging off the sides like limbs) is essentially just one giant tube. Topologically, this makes perfect sense. Back in the earliest days of animal life, some organisms tried a flat design, like a pancake, with digestion done on one side. Others tried a little pocket, with the same opening serving as entrance and exit. But the one-way tube proved to be the most successful, because it allowed our ancestors to process their last meal while eating their next. Those early creatures would travel through the world mouth first, which is why the sensory equipment evolved to be gathered around that end, with a brain nearby to make sense of everything. Hannah Fry: I lost my dad to Alzheimer’s. New research into its origins is amazing My lovely father died of Alzheimer’s last year, and since then, I’ve been digging into the disease to try to understand what happened to him. I was astonished to discover that scientists think it may start in the nose, says New Scientist’s new columnist, Professor Hannah Fry Now, picture a human standing up, tilting their head back, to make them a nice straight tube, still without limbs (sorry, but this is what happens when you let a mathematician write a science column). The ears, eyes, nose and brain all sit together in a cluster, on what I’m going to call the north side of the digestive tube running through the middle. So if you were deciding where the lungs should go, you’d surely put them on the same side of the tube as the nose, tucked in next to the spine. That way, you would have a neat tube for air and another for food, both running side by side, and even a first-year engineering student could draw a diagram of it for you. Except that’s not where the lungs are. They ended up on the belly, or south, side of the body. Which leaves us with this topological monstrosity, where air that comes in through your nose has to cut straight across the path of your food to get to your lungs. And everything you eat has to cut straight back across the path of your air to get to your stomach. It would be like plumbing your gas main through the kitchen sink, fitting a little flap on top and trusting you to remember to shut it every time you do the washing up. The reason for this mess is a fish . More than 420 million years ago, long before anything with a backbone had crawled onto land, a fish started gulping air at the surface. A little pouch on the belly side of its gut, just underneath the mouth, got better and better at soaking up oxygen, and that pouch became a lung. That fish became the ancestor of every mammal , bird, amphibian and reptile on Earth. And because evolution is about being as lazy as you can possibly be without dying, the lungs stayed exactly where they were. The extraordinary ways species control their own evolutionary fate Natural selection isn’t just something that happens to organisms, their activities also play a role, giving some species – including humans – a supercharged ability to evolve So why didn’t the nose move instead? Swivel it round so it sits under the mouth on your chin and you have a much more mathematically pleasing face. Unfortunately, the smell cells are wired straight into the front of the brain, so move the nose and the brain has to come along with it. There’s just no wiggle room. One end of your airway was anchored by your sense of smell, the other was fixed by an accident over 420 million years ago, and your throat is the bodge job evolution came up with to make it all work. Snakes have a tube behind their tongue that they can use like a snorkel so that they can still breathe even when swallowing a whole deer in one go. Toothed whales have two completely separate tubes that twirl into position like waterslides. Most mammals, including dogs and cats, have a voice box that sits right up at the top of the throat, poking up into the back of the nose, and tubes for food that flow round either side of the wind pipe to the stomach. Read more Why honing your sense of smell could keep you sharp as you age Human babies start off that way too, which is why they can suckle and breathe at the same time. But in the first six months of life, the human larynx drops down the neck , unplugging the airway from the back of the nose and leaving it wide open to whatever comes in from the mouth. What’s left is a very human oddity. A single, shared chamber sitting low down at the back of your throat that is great for speaking, but does require your vocal folds to slam shut, the epiglottis to come down like a trapdoor and your airway to be sealed off every time you swallow. As a result, humans have the questionable honour of being one of the few animals on Earth for whom every single mouthful is a potentially lethal exercise in anatomical coordination. Other animals can choke, sure, but our strange anatomy makes us the most vulnerable to choking of all mammals. Which is how roughly 162,000 people die globally each year. But evolution, having left us in this mess, did at least make the trapdoor almost impossible to switch off. The surgeon – mid mime – told me that when he is in people’s throats performing surgery, the EEG monitor reading can be measuring almost no brain activity. Still, any little tickle in the throat and those folds will slam shut. As you can imagine, I spent the rest of the party watching the children eat their cake very, very carefully. None of them choked, which, given the state of the plumbing, is frankly a miracle. Read more Hannah Fry: How to win The Traitors with maths (step one, don’t get made a traitor)

item.title: Watch live: Europe unveils 1st close-up views of asteroid Dimorphos after NASA's DART impact
item.description: null After a two-year journey, the Hera spacecraft is arriving at the Didymos double asteroid system, and its first images are being released to the public today (Nov. 25). The European Space Agency's (ESA's ) Hera probe launched atop a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station on Oct. 7, 2024 . Its destination is the Didymos-Dimorphos asteroid system, which consists of the larger Didymos , a " rubble pile" asteroid , and its smaller moonlet Dimorphos. NASA slammed a kinetic impactor into Dimorphos in 2022 in the historic DART test , which confirmed that such an impact can alter the trajectory of an asteroid. Hera arrives at Didymos today, and ESA is sharing the first close-up images from the mission in a free online livestream. ESA's livestream starts at 1:45 p.m. ET (1845 GMT) on Wednesday (Nov. 25) . Watch it live here, courtesy of the European Space Agency. At Dimorphos, Hera will inspect the wreckage caused by DART (Double Asteroid Redirect Test), humanity's first test of planetary defense. The test was designed to see if the orbit of a threatening asteroid could be altered, taking it off a potential crash course with Earth. A simulation of the impact of DART on Didymos (Image credit: S.D. Raducan) The DART mission succeeded, shortening Dimorphos' orbit by just over 30 minutes, showing that kinetic impacts can indeed alter the trajectories of asteroids. Hera will now show up to the crash scene and study the impact crater left by DART and inspect any changes the collision caused. Scientists are thrilled by the prospects. A series of images captured by the DART spacecraft as it sped to impact the asteroid Dimorphos on Sept. 26, 2022. (Image credit: NASA/JHUAPL) "ESA's Hera mission has arrived to learn the answers we need to know," the mission's principal investigator Patrick Michel said in an ESA statement . "How did the impact change Dimorphos? What is the mass of the asteroid and which of its properties explain its response to DART impact? "Hera is carrying out a thorough investigation ever of a deflected asteroid, packed with scientific firsts, to give us a complete and unbiased picture of humankind's first planetary defense test." A view of Didymos from ESA's Hera spacecraft.
