item.dc:creator: Brett Tingley
item.content:encoded: null After a two-year journey, the Hera spacecraft is arriving at the Didymos double asteroid system, and its first images are being released to the public today (Nov. 25). The European Space Agency's (ESA's ) Hera probe launched atop a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station on Oct. 7, 2024 . Its destination is the Didymos-Dimorphos asteroid system, which consists of the larger Didymos , a " rubble pile" asteroid , and its smaller moonlet Dimorphos. NASA slammed a kinetic impactor into Dimorphos in 2022 in the historic DART test , which confirmed that such an impact can alter the trajectory of an asteroid. Hera arrives at Didymos today, and ESA is sharing the first close-up images from the mission in a free online livestream. ESA's livestream starts at 1:45 p.m. ET (1845 GMT) on Wednesday (Nov. 25) . Watch it live here, courtesy of the European Space Agency. At Dimorphos, Hera will inspect the wreckage caused by DART (Double Asteroid Redirect Test), humanity's first test of planetary defense. The test was designed to see if the orbit of a threatening asteroid could be altered, taking it off a potential crash course with Earth. A simulation of the impact of DART on Didymos (Image credit: S.D. Raducan) The DART mission succeeded, shortening Dimorphos' orbit by just over 30 minutes, showing that kinetic impacts can indeed alter the trajectories of asteroids. Hera will now show up to the crash scene and study the impact crater left by DART and inspect any changes the collision caused. Scientists are thrilled by the prospects. A series of images captured by the DART spacecraft as it sped to impact the asteroid Dimorphos on Sept. 26, 2022. (Image credit: NASA/JHUAPL) "ESA's Hera mission has arrived to learn the answers we need to know," the mission's principal investigator Patrick Michel said in an ESA statement . "How did the impact change Dimorphos? What is the mass of the asteroid and which of its properties explain its response to DART impact? "Hera is carrying out a thorough investigation ever of a deflected asteroid, packed with scientific firsts, to give us a complete and unbiased picture of humankind's first planetary defense test." A view of Didymos from ESA's Hera spacecraft. (Image credit: ESA) ESA has already shared some of the remarkable images Hera has captured en route to Didymos, including a breathtaking image of both asteroids as Dimorphos cast its shadow on its larger companion in a deep-space double-asteroid solar eclipse . Hera even stopped by Mars on its way to the asteroids, snapping pictures of its moon Deimos . The image shows the Didymos double asteroid system, which consists of the larger Didymos and its moonlet, Dimorphos. In this image, Dimorphos' shadow can be seen on the surface of Didymos. (Image credit: ESA) Hera will remain at the Didymos-Dimorphos system for months, deploying cubesats that will study the asteroids with visible and infrared light cameras and radar instruments. Through Hera, scientists hope to refine planetary defense techniques so that, should the time ever come, humanity has options for defending itself against incoming space rocks like the one that wiped out the dinosaurs 66 million years ago . "Through many years of hard work our international collaboration managed to do just that, and for the very highest of intentions: to help make Earth safer," said Hera mission manager Ian Carnelli.

item.title: Xteink’s pocketable X4 Classic e-reader is down to just $55 for Black Friday
item.description: Unsurprisingly, we’re already seeing some solid Black Friday deals on a wide variety of e-readers. Everything from the Kobo Libra Colour to last-gen Kindle Paperwhite is on sale, but if you’re looking for something much cheaper — or considerably smaller — the Xteink X4 Classic is in a league of its own. Thankfully, the tiny e-reader is down to a new low of $54.87 ($55 off) at Amazon , making it an especially affordable alternative to Amazon’s latest Kindle. Xteink X4 Classic pocket e-reader Where to Buy: $109 $54.87 at Amazon (black) $109 $54.87 at Amazon (white) $109 $59 at Xteink The X4 Classic is an updated version of Xteink’s original pocket-sized e-reader, one that features a miniature 4.3-inch E Ink display that makes it more pocketable than any current Kindle or Kobo model. Like the pricier X4 Pro — which also happens to be on sale direct from Xteink for $84 — it features both physical page-turning buttons and magnets that let you attach it to compatible smartphones. At just 2.4 ounces and 4.9mm thick, it’s also easy to slip into a pocket, while its larger 920mAh battery can last up to 10 days on a single charge. That said, unlike the X4 Pro , the Classic lacks a touchscreen and built-in reading light, meaning you’ll need an external light to read in the dark. It also uses a proprietary magnetic charging connector instead of USB-C, and transferring books isn’t as straightforward as on a Kindle or Kobo. However, like the Pro, it does support the excellent CrossPoint Reader software , which you can install yourself to improve the reading experience. You can even use it to read books borrowed through Libby or purchased from stores like Kobo, though it takes a few extra steps to do so. Still, if you want an inexpensive, distraction-free way to read on the go, the X4 Classic is hard to beat for less than half the price of a Kindle. Read our hands-on impressions of the Xteink X4.

item.title: Colombian authorities rescue all hostages held at Cartagena supermarket
item.description: Security forces rescued all the hostages held for nearly a day at a supermarket in the northern Colombian tourist city of Cartagena, President Abelardo de la Espriella said early Wednesday. The president said that the men were “common criminals” who fled into the supermarket after a failed attempt to hold up an armored truck. The hostage situation broke out as Colombia is experiencing a wave of attacks by rebel groups on government targets.

item.description: …Give NSCDC seven days to submit operational records By Gift Cnapi-Odekina, Abuja ABUJA — The House of Representatives Committee on Solid Minerals Development has asked the Commander of the Mining Marshals, ACC Attah John Onoja, to tender a written apology to the National Assembly over the contents of a letter concerning a member of the House, Hon. Abdulmalik Danga. The committee also gave the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) seven days to submit outstanding operational records relating to petitions on the activities of the Mining Marshals, including complaints about arrests, detention of mining operators and the closure of mining sites. The decisions followed an investigative hearing chaired by Hon. Jonathan Gaza, during which lawmakers sought clarification from Onoja over a July 24, 2026 letter addressed to the Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas. The letter concerned the intervention of Danga, who represents Adavi/Okehi Federal Constituency of Kogi State, in matters relating to the activities of the Mining Marshals. In the correspondence, Onoja expressed reservations about the lawmaker’s intervention, linking it to concerns surrounding the enforcement of regulations against illegal mining. item.dc:creator: Nwafor
item.content:encoded: …Give NSCDC seven days to submit operational records By Gift Cnapi-Odekina, Abuja ABUJA — The House of Representatives Committee on Solid Minerals Development has asked the Commander of the Mining Marshals, ACC Attah John Onoja, to tender a written apology to the National Assembly over the contents of a letter concerning a member of the House, Hon. Abdulmalik Danga. The committee also gave the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) seven days to submit outstanding operational records relating to petitions on the activities of the Mining Marshals, including complaints about arrests, detention of mining operators and the closure of mining sites. The decisions followed an investigative hearing chaired by Hon. Jonathan Gaza, during which lawmakers sought clarification from Onoja over a July 24, 2026 letter addressed to the Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas. The letter concerned the intervention of Danga, who represents Adavi/Okehi Federal Constituency of Kogi State, in matters relating to the activities of the Mining Marshals. In the correspondence, Onoja expressed reservations about the lawmaker’s intervention, linking it to concerns surrounding the enforcement of regulations against illegal mining. Reading an excerpt from the letter, Gaza said the language used in the correspondence raised concerns about the manner in which a serving member of the National Assembly was addressed. The letter stated: “While we respect the rules of lawmaking in shaping the society through oversight legislative functions, we strongly view the action of Abdulmalik Danga as anti-government and motivated by illegal mining cartels whose unlawful activities are being disrupted by the sanity being restored in the mining sector.” The committee members questioned the basis for the assertions and whether the correspondence reflected an authorised institutional position of the NSCDC. Responding, Onoja told the committee that he wrote the letter in his personal capacity as Commander of the Mining Marshals and did not intend to challenge the constitutional powers of the legislature. He said: “Mr. Chairman, permit me to state clearly on record. My response, my letter, in my personal capacity as the Commander Mining Marshals, is not in any way looking into the legislative powers of the Committee. The letter is speaking to the motion as moved.” Gaza, however, questioned the explanation, particularly because the correspondence was written on NSCDC letterhead and carried an official reference number. The committee chairman consequently asked the NSCDC Commandant-General, Ahmed Abubakar Audi, to clarify whether the letter represented the official position of the Corps or was issued without institutional authorisation. Audi said the Corps had administrative procedures requiring officers to obtain approval before issuing correspondence on behalf of the Commandant-General. He explained that an officer authorised to communicate on behalf of the Commandant-General would sign such a letter in the latter’s name. Audi said the letter under review did not follow that format, adding that Onoja had signed it in his personal capacity. “According to our administrative procedure, if an officer is instructed to write a letter on behalf of the CG, the officer will sign that letter for the Commandant-General. But if you check the letter, you’ll see that there’s no… So he signed it on his own personal capacity,” Audi said. The committee maintained that the use of official stationery and reference details required further clarification regarding the circumstances in which the correspondence was issued. Reps demand outstanding operational records In a separate development, the committee expressed concern over the non-submission of documents it had requested from the NSCDC concerning the operations of the Mining Marshals. Gaza recalled that the committee, on October 20, 2026, issued a formal request for documentary records and a notice requiring the personal appearance of the Commandant-General. The directive requested a comprehensive response verified on oath, alongside 10 properly bound and paginated hard copies and an identical electronic copy of the relevant primary documents. The committee said the November 3 deadline passed without the requested documents and written response being submitted. Gaza explained that the records were required to assist the committee in examining petitions and complaints concerning the enforcement activities of the Mining Marshals, including reported arrests, detention of mining operators and the handling of mining sites. He said the Commandant-General’s appearance before the committee did not remove the Corps’ obligation to provide the requested documents. “Let it be clear on the record that personal attendance does not cure or waive the statutory obligation to produce primary, certified, and unedited documentary records within the possession, custody, or control of the Corps,” he said. The committee subsequently directed the Commandant-General, the Mining Marshals commander and all zonal, state and FCT commands to preserve records relating to their enforcement operations. The requested records include mining site inspection reports, arrest and custody registers, operational logs, financial and banking records, vehicle registers, electronic metadata, official correspondence and CCTV recordings across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory. Gaza cautioned against any alteration, concealment, removal or destruction of relevant records, as well as any action that could interfere with the committee’s investigation or intimidate officers and witnesses. Citing Section 14 of the Legislative Houses (Powers and Privileges) Act, 2017, and Section 19 of the NSCDC Act, he said the committee would consider appropriate statutory measures where necessary. At the end of the proceedings, the committee asked Onoja to issue a written apology to the National Assembly over the contents of his letter concerning Danga and directed the NSCDC to submit the outstanding records within seven days. Mining operators present complaints Meanwhile, some mining stakeholders who appeared before the committee raised concerns about the enforcement activities of the Mining Marshals. The operators alleged that some mining businesses had been subjected to arrests, detention of personnel and closure of sites, including operations they said were covered by licences issued by the Ministry of Solid Minerals Development. They also complained that enforcement actions had disrupted their businesses and resulted in financial losses, with some operators claiming that equipment and machinery had remained idle following the closure of their sites. The stakeholders called on the committee to examine the complaints and establish whether the enforcement actions in question complied with applicable laws and regulatory procedures. They urged the relevant authorities to ensure that disputes over mining licences and compliance were addressed through established regulatory and legal channels. The operators further called for greater transparency in enforcement operations and safeguards for businesses operating with valid approvals. They maintained that efforts to curb illegal mining should be accompanied by adherence to due process and respect for the rights of mining operators. The complaints were presented as part of the issues before the committee and remain subject to its investigation. The post Reps seek clarification over mining marshals’ letter to lawmaker appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Violence against women in the digital age: When the internet becomes a weapon
item.description: November 25th is the United Nation's International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women. In the age of social media and artificial intelligence, there are now new spaces in which violence against women has appeared, with the internet now a growing weapon in the hands of abusers. 85% of women who spend time online have witnessed violence, and 38% have been the target of it.

item.title: Debian wakes up wearing Windows XP's actual skin
item.description: Win4Wine is one of the more remarkable and creative hacks we've read about in recent years. It runs Windows XP's genuine Explorer shell through patched Wine on Debian 13, with a custom window manager integrating Linux applications into the desktop. As its GitHub repository explains: "The taskbar, Start menu, desktop and folder windows are XP's real ones, and Linux applications get XP's frames and taskbar buttons." This impressive, possibly demented project has English installation instructions and a README, although its design documents are in Japanese. We found Mozilla's built-in translation handled those pretty well. Its developer goes by miKuta0407 on GitHub, their homepage , and X . Also note, you're going to need some Windows installation media for the full experience. The README says: "No Microsoft files are included. Only the files that are needed are extracted locally from your own ISO." It supports Windows XP Professional SP3 installation images in 32-bit Japanese or English editions, with an experimental option for Windows 7 SP1 x64. Without either Windows image, it can download and use ReactOS's free software shell instead, for what it terms "a Windows 2000-like classic look." In our view, that sounds much better anyway. Before any former Windows users cry hurray and reach for an optical drive, this is not some ready-to-run project. The top of the README warns: "This is a personal, experimental project, not a finished product for daily use." The developer has tested it only on a fresh Debian 13 installation and recommends a VM or spare machine, rather than an existing working desktop, which sounds like an excellent precaution to us. Also, before you ask, yes, it was vibe-coded with Claude. We found ourselves reminded of another crazy-but-is-it project that we wrote about back in January: What if Linux ran Windows... and meant it? Meet Loss32 . The Loss32 proposal was even more extreme. It suggested replacing essentially the entire Linux userland, so it would be a Linux kernel running Wine with a Windows desktop and Windows apps. However, Mikuta-san was way ahead of us – lower down, the README mentions and even links to Loss32. Saying that, since it launched at the end of 2025, the bottom of the Loss32 web page shows a couple of updates, reporting on delays in getting it working. That, to be honest, did not shock us, but we still admire the let's-do-this spirit. The developer also seems to have got slightly distracted by a previous project, touchHLE: high-level emulator for early iOS apps . Loss32, in turn, reminded us of Neptune OS, an attempt to give seL4 a Windows personality transplant . We wrote about that back in 2022, and work on it has continued: the project page shows updates in recent months. The team has also pushed out preview releases in 2022, 2024, 2025, and most recently in September. This OS face transplant also reminded us of our article, Classic 7 is Windows 10 LTSC cosplaying as Windows 7 . Some people really miss the

item.title: US army to detonate stockpile of unstable bomb-making chemicals in Iowa
item.description: The US military will on Wednesday detonate some 10,000 pounds of unstable and degraded explosive material in Iowa, where local residents were urged to evacuate amid concerns over possible toxic lead contamination. US officials say the 68 drums of lead azide are at risk of spontaneous explosion. A series of safety measures are being taken to curb potential contamination from the blast, but the Army has encouraged residents of a small town and other nearby areas to leave "out of an abundance of caution."

item.title: The forgotten victims of femicide: Children orphaned by violence in Italy
item.description: November 25th is International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women. The forgotten victims of femicide are the children who find themselves motherless, often because their mother was killed by their own father. Italy recorded 97 female homicides in 2025 – 62 of them were committed by a partner. These crimes leave whole families devastated and children who have to grow up without their parents. FRANCE 24’s correspondent in Italy, Natalia Mendoza, reports.

item.content:encoded: November 25th is International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women. The forgotten victims of femicide are the children who find themselves motherless, often because their mother was killed by their own father. Italy recorded 97 female homicides in 2025 – 62 of them were committed by a partner. These crimes leave whole families devastated and children who have to grow up without their parents. FRANCE 24’s correspondent in Italy, Natalia Mendoza, reports.

item.title: Nollywood Stars Joke Silva, Funke Akindele, Others Pay Tribute To Pete Edochie
item.description: Nollywood stars Joke Silva, Funke Akindele, Mercy Johnson and others have paid tributes to veteran actor Pete Edochie, who died Wednesday after a prolonged battle with prostate cancer at the age of 79. The actor’s death was announced by his son, Chief Leo Pete Edochie, who confirmed that he died at 12:30 a.m. on November 25, 2026, in Enugu, Nigeria. His death has sparked an outpouring of tributes from colleagues, public leaders and entertainers who have celebrated his remarkable career, influence and legacy. Actress Joke Silva expressed sadness over his death, remembering his playful side. “Uncle Pete…I will miss your teasing. Rest well Sir,” she wrote. Filmmaker and actress Funke Akindele recalled growing up watching Edochie in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart , before eventually sharing the screen with him in the film Egg of Life . She expressed gratitude for his encouragement and the impact he made on younger generations of actors. “Thank you for paving the way for so many of us in Nollywood and for being an inspiration to us over the years. Your work lives on,” she wrote. Similarly, actress Uche Jombo described Edochie as one of Nollywood’s greatest pillars, a master of his craft and a custodian of Nigerian culture. She said the late actor “gave Nigerian storytelling a face, a voice and a legacy that will outlive generations.” “His contribution to Nollywood cannot be measured by the number of films he appeared in, but by the impact he made, the standards he set and the generations of actors he inspired.” Actress Omoni Oboli described his passing as the fall of an iroko tree, writing, “Hmmm 2026! It is well. The Iroko has fallen. Rest in power sir Pete Edochie.” May Edochie, the estranged wife of the late actor’s son, Yul Edochie, also paid tribute, describing him as an institution and a father figure to many. She reflected on the false reports of his death that had circulated over the years, noting that he had continued working despite the rumours. Actor Charles Inojie paid tribute using several of the late actor’s traditional praise names, including Ebube Dike, Ntu Mara Igwe and King of the Forests, before praying for his peaceful rest. While DJ Kaywise thanked him for his contributions to the industry, other entertainers who expressed their grief included comedian Sabinus, who described Edochie as an oracle and a legend. Pete Edochie was born on March 7, 1947, in Zaria, Kaduna State. His ancestral roots, however, trace back to Akamnato, Ifite Nteje, in Anambra State. Edochie rose to prominence through his portrayal of Okonkwo in the 1987 Nigerian Television Authority adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart . His commanding screen presence, distinctive voice, and memorable delivery of traditional proverbs subsequently made him one of Nollywood’s most recognisable figures. Beyond his acting career, Edochie was also celebrated for his contributions to broadcasting and his influence on generations of Nigeri

item.title: Ebola Fight Runs Up Against Customs, Rites In Remote DR Congo
item.description: For health workers in the volatile eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), tackling local suspicions is as big a problem as combating the Ebola virus that has plagued it for six months. In the rural community of Bulambo-Isale, AFP saw a small crowd gather this week along a dirt track, determined to prevent an ambulance bringing the body of a local Ebola victim for burial. Victims of the highly contagious haemorrhagic fever, which spreads through direct contact with bodily fluids, must be interred in sealed body bags to prevent infection spreading from the corpse. Burial ceremonies are conducted by specially trained health workers, anonymous in protective hazmat suits, some of whom locals allege are brought in from outside the community and do not speak the local languages. In this file photo taken on March 09, 2019 Health workers are seen inside the ‘red zone’ of an Ebola treatment centre, which was attacked in the early hours of the morning in Butembo. – Democratic Republic of Congo’s government on June 25, 2020 officially declared an end to an epidemic of Ebola that broke out in the east of the troubled country in August 2018 and went on to claim 2,277 lives. (Photo by JOHN WESSELS / AFP) But custom dictates that the deceased be buried by their own family and their body be allowed to fuse with the earth of their ancestors. “The authorities have imposed the Ebola response on locals without first making sure how they interpret it,” grumbled Patricien Kambale, who became a livestock farmer after university. “The sick victim gets carted away in a vehicle and locals don’t know where they’re being taken. Then we learn later that the person has died so locals think the doctors are using poisoned medicine to kill people,” he said. Suspicions of ‘profiteering’ Health workers in Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) simulate with the help of an Outbreak Response Advisor admission protocols of suspected cases during a training by medical charity, Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) to reinforce regional emergency response capacity for Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo Locals say they are distrustful of Congolese authorities, who have a reputation for corruption and nepotism. Left to cope with the miseries inflicted by myriad armed groups that have stalked their mineral-rich region for more than three decades, they fear their customs and lives matter little to the powers that be. Wilson Kasyani, chief doctor for the Vuhovi health district that includes Bulambo-Isale, a rural settlement in North Kivu province, was worried for the ambulance and its occupants. “Weapons are everywhere” in the mountainous region, he said. Medical workers face almost daily attacks due to locals’ hostility to efforts to respond to the Ebola outbreak, which has killed more than 5,000 people out of more than 11,000 cases since May. “Today, people entered a nurse’s home and wounded her son,” Kasyani said wearily. “And yesterday we had to stop someone who wanted to attack invest

item.content:encoded: For health workers in the volatile eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), tackling local suspicions is as big a problem as combating the Ebola virus that has plagued it for six months. In the rural community of Bulambo-Isale, AFP saw a small crowd gather this week along a dirt track, determined to prevent an ambulance bringing the body of a local Ebola victim for burial. Victims of the highly contagious haemorrhagic fever, which spreads through direct contact with bodily fluids, must be interred in sealed body bags to prevent infection spreading from the corpse. Burial ceremonies are conducted by specially trained health workers, anonymous in protective hazmat suits, some of whom locals allege are brought in from outside the community and do not speak the local languages. In this file photo taken on March 09, 2019 Health workers are seen inside the ‘red zone’ of an Ebola treatment centre, which was attacked in the early hours of the morning in Butembo. – Democratic Republic of Congo’s government on June 25, 2020 officially declared an end to an epidemic of Ebola that broke out in the east of the troubled country in August 2018 and went on to claim 2,277 lives. (Photo by JOHN WESSELS / AFP) But custom dictates that the deceased be buried by their own family and their body be allowed to fuse with the earth of their ancestors. “The authorities have imposed the Ebola response on locals without first making sure how they interpret it,” grumbled Patricien Kambale, who became a livestock farmer after university. “The sick victim gets carted away in a vehicle and locals don’t know where they’re being taken. Then we learn later that the person has died so locals think the doctors are using poisoned medicine to kill people,” he said. Suspicions of ‘profiteering’ Health workers in Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) simulate with the help of an Outbreak Response Advisor admission protocols of suspected cases during a training by medical charity, Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) to reinforce regional emergency response capacity for Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo Locals say they are distrustful of Congolese authorities, who have a reputation for corruption and nepotism. Left to cope with the miseries inflicted by myriad armed groups that have stalked their mineral-rich region for more than three decades, they fear their customs and lives matter little to the powers that be. Wilson Kasyani, chief doctor for the Vuhovi health district that includes Bulambo-Isale, a rural settlement in North Kivu province, was worried for the ambulance and its occupants. “Weapons are everywhere” in the mountainous region, he said. Medical workers face almost daily attacks due to locals’ hostility to efforts to respond to the Ebola outbreak, which has killed more than 5,000 people out of more than 11,000 cases since May. “Today, people entered a nurse’s home and wounded her son,” Kasyani said wearily. “And yesterday we had to stop someone who wanted to attack investigators with a machete.” A mock coffin bearing the words “Reject Ebola” abandoned by protesters lies in a street amid tear gas fired by Kenyan police officers during a demonstration against a controversial US-built Ebola quarantine centre slated to begin operations at Laikipia Air Base in Nanyuki on June 9, 2026. Photo by LUIS TATO / AFP Roland Vivaya, head of the local youth council, said “most people” in Bulambo-Isale “don’t believe Ebola exists”. He admitted he hadn’t “really” believed himself until he almost died of the virus. Vivaya said the difficulty was not so much defiance but locals not understanding — despite memories of the last Ebola outbreak between 2018 and 2000. The image at the time of “doctors protected by the military, scared the community”, Kambale said. No vaccine or specific treatment currently exists for the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, responsible for the current outbreak. “How can you explain to locals — many of whom have never been to school — why there’s this sudden focus on this disease, when we’ve been dying for decades from the conflicts here,” Vivaya said. “Personally, I only understood the virus when I had to go to the treatment centre, because they put on information sessions. But these meetings don’t get the message across to everyone,” he added ruefully. Suspicions stem, in part, from health workers having not been trained in local customs or languages, leading to “resistance” among locals, he said. “They think it might be some kind of profiteering,” Vivaya added. Communicate with the dead Marie-Therese Tsesi, a 63-year-old nurse, folds clothing at her home with one of her adopted five children orphaned by the Ebola outbreak in Mongbwalu, north eastern Democratic Republic of Congo October 11, 2026.(Photo by MARIE RUWET / AFP) Bulambo-Isale is the cultural and religious heart of the Nande people, one of the eastern DRC’s largest ethnic groups. From his palm-frond hut, blackened by wood smoke, traditional chief Pimbo Kakule watches, pipe clenched between his teeth, over one of Bulambo-Isale’s 12 sacred hills. As in many rural communities affected by Ebola, the fight to staunch its spread runs up against ancient traditions. “Our people believe there is life after death and our customs must be respected when a person is buried. Otherwise we think they’ve been sacrificed,” he said. Nande custom dictates that a person should be buried by their family and their corpse enter the soil of their ancestors so the living can speak to them in the afterlife. “A person who isn’t able to communicate with their dead can’t get into heaven,” Kakule said. He said there were better ways to manage the issue than the current top-down approach. “If we were to say: ‘Your brother’s died. We’re going to teach you how to bury him,’ we might reach an agreement and there wouldn’t be all this tension,” he said. “We are fighting the disease, not the response teams.” Top down or bottom up A hygienist wearing personal protective equipment (PPE) begins cleaning and disinfection operations at the Rwampara Ebola Treatment Centre (ETC) in Bunia, Ituri, in the east of the Democratic Republic of Congo on July 13, 2026. The salaries that some locally recruited people are offered for joining the Ebola fight is also a source of mistrust. Their wages, higher than the local average, feed jealousy and conspiracy theories. When Kambale was vaccinated in 2020 against the Zaire strain of Ebola, responsible for the epidemic of the time, his neighbours accused him of taking a bribe in order to spread the virus and threatened to torch his house. “Even protecting yourself has become a problem,” he said. “Pressure groups” made up of members of youth organisations linked to local politicians, weaponise the tensions and sometimes prevent health workers reaching sick people. In Vuhovi, such incidents are often the work of troublemakers who feel marginalised, said Salama Mwengesyali, who coordinates public Ebola information sessions. “If we could bring all these individuals in, train them and get them involved in tackling Ebola, we could overcome this resistance,” the soft-spoken woman said. “What we lack are the means to do that.” Mwengesyali said her team lacked money to “motivate” locals in rural farming communities to attend lengthy Ebola information sessions, or pay health workers to ring them or travel to where they live. “It’s come down to us having to go door to door to plead for body bags,” concurred Kasyani, the doctor. Their Ebola treatment centre is cobbled together from planks of wood where patients “put up with intolerable conditions”, he said. Two patients have run away in recent days. “People tell themselves that if they go there, they’re going to die.” The post Ebola Fight Runs Up Against Customs, Rites In Remote DR Congo appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Astronomers discover the most distant and ancient supermassive black hole-powered quasar in the universe
item.description: null The Euclid space telescope has spotted the most distant and ancient quasar ever seen, a bright cosmic event powered by a supermassive black hole with 360 million times the mass of the sun. The supermassive black hole is seen as it was just 630 million years after the Big Bang. 40 million years further back in time than the previous record holder for the most ancient quasar. The discovery further deepens the mystery of how supermassive black holes grew so massive so soon into the history of the universe. That's because previously, scientists had theorized it should take 1 billion years of feeding and merging for black holes to reach supermassive status of millions or billions of times as massive as the sun. Quasars occur when supermassive black holes are surrounded by vast amounts of gas and dust on which they feed. The immense gravitational influence of the black hole causes this material, in the form of an accretion disk, to glow brightly and to blast out bright jets of plasma. That means quasars at the heart of galaxies in regions called active galactic nuclei (AGNs) like this one can often be brighter than the combined light of every star in the entire surrounding galaxy, but only briefly. The newly discovered quasar, designated J1504+6252 and nicknamed Dún Aonghasa, is in this brief phase of its existence. It was discovered among millions of objects in 18 months of data from Euclid. Euclid's initial observation of Dún Aonghasa was followed up by an array of ground-based and space-based telescopes, including the W.M. Keck Observatory, the Large Binocular Telescope Observatory, the Hubble Space Telescope , and ultimately the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). It was the JWST that determined the mass of this supermassive black hole. What is interesting about Dún Aonghasa is that it is unlike other supermassive black holes seen at a similar period of the early universe. That's because this black hole is feeding relatively slowly. That means if it engaged in rapid feeding to reach its massive size, that period of gorging on gas and dust has either ended or it has paused. The red dot at the center of this Euclid image is Dún Aonghasa (Image credit: ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA, Wolf et al. 2026) That is something that further complicates our picture of supermassive black hole growth. By staring back 13.1 billion years in time to see Dún Aonghasa, Euclid is also observing a crucial time in cosmic history when the first stars and galaxies were taking shape, and the clearing of cosmic gas was ending the dark ages of our universe by allowing light to travel freely. Euclid's primary mission is improving our understanding of dark energy , the mysterious force accelerating the expansion of the universe, and dark matter , the most mysterious "stuff" in the cosmos. Collectively, these aspects of the universe account for around 95% of its matter-energy budget and have come to be collectively referred to as the dark universe. Hence Euclid's nickname

item.title: Has vibe coding made open source the new normal for synths?
item.description: The emergence of powerful vibe-coding agents and tools like Reverse Engineer Anything has caused chaos in the music gear world , leaving companies scrambling to figure out how to respond. While some, like Roland, have remained silent for now, others have embraced the modding community. In the last several weeks, as it's become clear that no piece of music gear is safe from Claude and a subreddit full of curious tinkerers, companies have begun making more and more of their devices open source. item.title: ‘He’s more elegant’: Bellingham downplays Zidane comparisons after wondergoal
item.description: Englishman hailed by teammates and manager Mourinho after coming on to completely change Champions League game against PSV Eindhoven “It was one of those moments when you’re just: ‘Wow.’” Bernardo Silva had a good view of Jude Bellingham scoring the goal, the golazo , that put Real Madrid into the lead and the Bernabéu on its feet, shock giving way to song, naa, naa, naa, na-na-na-naa, na-na-na-naa ringing round again. “I have no idea what I did,” the Englishman said afterwards. What he did was turn all Le Tissier. Lifting the ball with his left, raising it with his right, twisting and not letting it drop, he sent it arching from the outside of his boot into the far corner, something straight out of the 90s. “I just kind of hit it,” Bellingham reckoned; not wanting to hit it too hard, it had gone “looping”, “stabbing”, he said. “Normally [my goals are] a lot closer, aren’t they? I was a bit surprised, honestly. Normally from there I’m looking to see who is an option to play it through to, but it popped up nicely. It was nice.” Nice? It was, Silva said, “special”. A “work of art” Marca called it. The presenter on one radio station claimed it was the best goal he had ever seen, and it wasn’t just him; wasn’t just the goal, either. Continue reading...

item.title: Israeli MPs advance bill for inquiry into security failings that led to October 7 Hamas attack
item.description: Israeli MPs on Wednesday gave their initial approval for the creation of a commission to investigate the security failures that led to the October 7, 2023 attack by Hamas. Caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who was in power when the attack happened, has repeatedly rejected calls to set up such a probe.

item.title: Producer and guitarist Ginton on jazz, remixing big hits and collaborating on a track for Drake
item.description: Amsterdam-based guitarist, DJ and music producer Ginton is known for blending reggae, Afro, Caribbean and electronic music. He also told us of his "surprise" in collaborating on a track for Drake's album "Honestly, Nevermind". He spoke to us in Perspective.

item.title: Senegal regaining Afcon title is the right end to embarrassing farrago but issues do not stop here | Osasu Obayiuwana
item.description: After African football was dragged into needless disrepute the next step is to tackle two key areas of governance A journey of 310 days and three legal proceedings to confirm two things we know – that Senegal beat Morocco 1-0 to win the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations and, most importantly, that the decision of a referee remains final and sacrosanct – has produced the longest, most comical and embarrassing Afcon final in the tournament’s 69-year history. As the Confederation of African Football (Caf) executive committee member Samir Sobha told the Guardian, the decision of the organisation’s appeals board in March to overturn Senegal’s victory and award the title to Morocco, prompting a legal charade ended by the court of arbitration for sport’s verdict on Tuesday , was a “big joke” that brought Caf and the Afcon into needless disrepute. Continue reading...

item.title: Microsoft 365 Backup stretches recovery window to ten years
item.description: Recovery windows of up to ten years are now available in Microsoft 365 Backup for OneDrive and SharePoint, up from a previous maximum of two. The change took effect on October 31, though Exchange remains capped at two years. Administrators can select recovery windows of three months, six months, or any whole number of years from one to ten. Microsoft's list price is $0.15 per GiB per month of protected content. Extended windows can increase costs by keeping deleted data billable for longer. Switching to a longer recovery window will also not make backups for that period magically available. So no nostalgic trips back to 2016. Wider recovery windows may appeal to organizations that need access to older data, but backups are not a substitute for compliance retention and archiving. Recovery after a breach or ransomware attack is also critical, particularly getting back to a healthy state before any malware seeped into files. Microsoft says backups are physically redundant and geographically replicated while respecting the tenant's data residency requirements. Full OneDrive account and SharePoint site restores offer recovery points every ten minutes for the most recent two weeks, then weekly points through the configured window, up to ten years. Individual file and folder recovery is limited to recovery points from the most recent 14 days, regardless of the configured window. Restore remains free, which is handy since regular testing is a vital part of any disaster recovery plan. The arrival of a ten-year recovery window is good for enterprises that need it and have deep enough pockets. However, it is important to keep in mind that being able to configure a longer recovery window doesn't constitute a disaster recovery plan in itself and may be overkill in many instances. Microsoft notes: "The existing one-year default recovery window remains unchanged. Longer recovery windows must be configured on the applicable backup policies." The company also recommends that users "review your organization's SharePoint and OneDrive backup requirements to determine whether longer recovery windows are needed." A decade of recovery history could be valuable. It also means a decade of data to account for when setting budgets, access controls, and retention policies. ®

item.title: Amazon to flog motors in Britain, but Prime won't deliver
item.description: Amazon is channeling its inner car salesman as it prepares to flog motors on the UK arm of its online tat bazaar. Amazon Autos will launch in Britain in early 2027, its first expansion outside the US, where it debuted in December 2024. Customers can browse and reserve cars online before completing the purchase with a dealer. Hoping it will be "a nice little earner," Amazon will let punters view real-time dealer inventory, prices, get an instant trade-in valuation, and connect with a local dealer to reserve a car, "all on Amazon." In the US, the service now covers more than 150 cities and offers vehicles from 35 brands. Hyundai is the first announced UK carmaker partner, while dealer group Vertu Motors will list used vehicles. More brands and dealers are due to be confirmed before launch. Hyundai's launch range will include electric, hybrid, and petrol models. "Buying a car is one of the biggest purchases people make, and we think it should feel as simple and transparent as shopping for anything on Amazon," said Matt Nuffort, director of Amazon Autos International. Of course, buying a car isn't quite like adding an air fryer or a memory stick to your basket. How does financing and checkout work for UK buyers? Customers will complete the purchase and paperwork at their chosen dealership. Amazon is not offering financing itself, but buyers can explore financing options via the site, adjusting terms like deposit and duration to see how monthly payments change. Credit applications must be completed with the dealer. In the US, buyers can submit a credit application through the platform, review terms and conditions, then sign electronic contracts online. They typically pay a deposit and visit the dealership to complete the remaining paperwork and pick up the vehicle. Buyers shouldn't expect their new car to arrive in an enormous cardboard box with a smiley logo on it, or to be lowered onto their driveway by a giant Amazon delivery drone. But given that one of the online retailer's flying delivery robots crashed into someone's garage after making a drop-off near Detroit last week, perhaps that's for the best. ®

item.title: Cardi B Wears Nigerian Designers Weiz Dhurm Franklyn & Sevon Dejana for Billboard Canada Cover
item.description: Cardi B in Nigerian Designers Sevon Dejana and Weiz Dhurm Franklyn for Billboard Canada Cardi B ‘s latest fashion moment comes with a lovely Nigerian connection, and we have two designers to celebrate! The rapper is the newest cover star of Billboard Canada, following her recognition as the inaugural Global Woman of the Year at the 2026 Billboard Canada Women in Music ceremony in Toronto on 24 November 2026. For the accompanying editorial, her longtime creative collaborator Kollin Carter worked with photographer AB+DM Studio to put together a series of looks, including two gorgeous creations from Nigerian fashion houses Weiz Dhurm Franklyn and Sevon Dejana. And BNers, both designers brought something very different to the spread. First up is a sculptural blue mermaid gown by Abelia Anaba Franklyn , the creative mind behind Weiz Dhurm Franklyn. The design comes from the brand’s Spring/Summer 2027 Ready-to-Wear collection, The Remembering (Ncheta), which draws inspiration from the artistry of ancient Igbo-Ukwu bronze works. Its fitted silhouette is covered in painterly blue textures across the bodice and hips, while an exaggerated organza ruffle frames the neckline and reappears at the hem. The layered, feather-like finish gives the gown an almost sculptural quality, making it a particularly interesting interpretation of the collection’s inspiration. Cardi B wears a sculptural blue mermaid gown from Nigerian fashion house Weiz Dhurm Franklyn’s Spring/Summer 2027 Ready-to-Wear collection, The Remembering (Ncheta), for her Billboard Canada editorial. Photo Credit: Weiz Dhurm Franklyn/Instagram Then comes Sevon Dejana, with a two-piece couture creation from the label’s Out of Body Haute Couture Spring/Summer 2027 collection. Cardi wears a structured, high-neck jacket with long sleeves and a matching skirt, both covered in intricate gold, red and wine-coloured crystals. Three-dimensional crimson floral details add another layer to the design, while a towering floral headpiece completes the look. Set against a lush botanical backdrop, the entire styling leans into the collection’s dramatic, otherworldly direction. Cardi B wears a crystal-embroidered structured jacket and skirt from Nigerian designer Sevon Dejana’s Out of Body Haute Couture Spring/Summer 2027 collection for Billboard Canada. Photo Credit: Sevon Dejana/Instagram Of course, there’s more to Cardi’s Billboard Canada cover story than the fashion. The Grammy-winning rapper also gets candid about life as a mother of four , working through self-doubt and making history with her sold-out Little Miss Drama arena tour across North America. Looking back on a year that has included the release of her chart-topping second album, Am I the Drama? , and new business ventures, she tells the magazine that the past twelve months have reminded her of who she is. The post Cardi B Wears Nigerian Designers Weiz Dhurm Franklyn & Sevon Dejana for Billboard Canada Cover appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Af

item.title: AI may soon change what it means to be a theoretical physicist
item.description: About six months ago, Suvrat Raju, a professor of theoretical physics at the International Centre for Theoretical Sciences in Bengaluru, India, asked a frontier AI model to solve a physics problem. He didn’t ask because he needed to know the answer. He had actually solved this particular problem already. But he had never published the solution—which made it a perfect question to test how good AI was at physics. LLMs have been trained on the whole Internet, so if a physics problem has been discussed online, it’s likely the model already knows about it and may have memorized the answer. So a fair test of AI capabilities needs to focus on problems that have never appeared online. The model didn’t answer Raju’s problem correctly, but it did better than he expected—well, enough to get him thinking that the experiment should be repeated and formalized. With the help of a colleague, he set out to create a theoretical physics benchmark for AI. Read full article Comments

item.title: Will Hajime Moriyasu get a high-profile job in Europe after his eight years in charge of Japan?
item.description: The coach will leave early after the postponement of the Asian Cup and, while there has been clear progress, some had hoped for better results at World Cups A popular Christmas tradition in Japan is to head to KFC but there is an unexpected item on the menu to chew over this year for the millions who do so – a meaty debate over Hajime Moriyasu’s eight years as national-team head coach. Among the many consequences of the Asian Cup’s postponement from January 2027 to December is the fact his tenure has ended early. The 58-year-old was supposed to stay on until February to cap that lengthy spell with (hopefully) a deserved trophy, hand over to Go Oiwa and then, perhaps, blaze a trail to Europe. Instead he left this month, after 113 games in charge during which Japan became a global force to be reckoned with, even if there are those who think he underdelivered. Continue reading...

item.title: November's full moon dazzles skywatchers with a stunning Beaver Moon supermoon (photos)
item.description: null The November full moon rose to put on a spectacular natural light show on Nov. 24 and we've got the photos to prove it! Read on to see our favorite shots of the "Beaver Moon" captured from around the world. Each monthly full moon has its own set of informal names , often bestowed to reflect events occurring in the world at the time of their rising. The November moon is often known as the Beaver Moon, a name associated with the time of year when beavers prepare for winter and when trappers historically set beaver traps before waterways froze. November's full moon served as the opening salvo in a series of four dazzling supermoons , which turn full around the time that the natural satellite passes closest to Earth in its 27-day elliptical orbit. That added proximity can make it appear noticeably brighter and larger than the smallest full moon of the year, setting the stage for an incredible photo shoot as the lunar disk climbed high into the autumn sky. Best photos of the November 2026 full Beaver Moon Our first shot of the moon was captured by photographer Pongmanat Tasiri as the moon rose over the roof of the Wat Phra That Doi Suthep Buddhist temple in Chiang Mai Province, Thailand, as a stunning array of craters and lunar seas scar the Beaver Moon's surface. The Beaver Moon takes flight into the night sky. (Image credit: Photo by Pongmanat Tasiri/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images) Meanwhile, Gary Hershorn snapped a gorgeous shot of the full yellow moon rising over the Chrysler Building in New York, with the Empire State Building and myriad other skyscrapers dominating the skyline. The Beaver Moon rises over the New York skyline. (Image credit: Photo by Gary Hershorn/Getty Images) Hershorn also managed to line up a colorful shot of the lunar disk glowing between the concrete canyon of New York's iconic 42nd Street just before moonset on the morning of Nov. 24, mere hours before the moon turned full. The moon shines between a concrete canyon in New York. (Image credit: Photo by Gary Hershorn/Getty Images) Our next photo was captured by Space.com's Skywatching Editor Daisy Dobrijevic using a Sony A7IV with a Tamron 50-400mm lens as the moon shone in the skies over the city of Nottingham in the U.K. on Nov. 23. "Having seen the rather disappointing weather forecast for the night of the full moon, I decided to head out a day early and capture the almost-full Beaver Moon instead," explained Dobrijevic. "It hadn’t quite risen above the rooftops of the houses opposite me, so I took a peek down the alleyway and, sure enough, there it was, nestled between two houses, giving me just enough of a clear view to capture this close-up." Bright ejecta rays stretch across ancient lunar lava plains in this close-up of the nearly full Beaver Moon captured from Nottingham, U.K. (Image credit: Daisy Dobrijevic) This striking image of the full moon rising above the Toronto skyline was snapped by Mert Alper Dervis as a flock of birds skimmed through the for
item.dc:creator: Anthony Wood
item.content:encoded: null The November full moon rose to put on a spectacular natural light show on Nov. 24 and we've got the photos to prove it! Read on to see our favorite shots of the "Beaver Moon" captured from around the world. Each monthly full moon has its own set of informal names , often bestowed to reflect events occurring in the world at the time of their rising. The November moon is often known as the Beaver Moon, a name associated with the time of year when beavers prepare for winter and when trappers historically set beaver traps before waterways froze. November's full moon served as the opening salvo in a series of four dazzling supermoons , which turn full around the time that the natural satellite passes closest to Earth in its 27-day elliptical orbit. That added proximity can make it appear noticeably brighter and larger than the smallest full moon of the year, setting the stage for an incredible photo shoot as the lunar disk climbed high into the autumn sky. Best photos of the November 2026 full Beaver Moon Our first shot of the moon was captured by photographer Pongmanat Tasiri as the moon rose over the roof of the Wat Phra That Doi Suthep Buddhist temple in Chiang Mai Province, Thailand, as a stunning array of craters and lunar seas scar the Beaver Moon's surface. The Beaver Moon takes flight into the night sky. (Image credit: Photo by Pongmanat Tasiri/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images) Meanwhile, Gary Hershorn snapped a gorgeous shot of the full yellow moon rising over the Chrysler Building in New York, with the Empire State Building and myriad other skyscrapers dominating the skyline. The Beaver Moon rises over the New York skyline. (Image credit: Photo by Gary Hershorn/Getty Images) Hershorn also managed to line up a colorful shot of the lunar disk glowing between the concrete canyon of New York's iconic 42nd Street just before moonset on the morning of Nov. 24, mere hours before the moon turned full. The moon shines between a concrete canyon in New York. (Image credit: Photo by Gary Hershorn/Getty Images) Our next photo was captured by Space.com's Skywatching Editor Daisy Dobrijevic using a Sony A7IV with a Tamron 50-400mm lens as the moon shone in the skies over the city of Nottingham in the U.K. on Nov. 23. "Having seen the rather disappointing weather forecast for the night of the full moon, I decided to head out a day early and capture the almost-full Beaver Moon instead," explained Dobrijevic. "It hadn’t quite risen above the rooftops of the houses opposite me, so I took a peek down the alleyway and, sure enough, there it was, nestled between two houses, giving me just enough of a clear view to capture this close-up." Bright ejecta rays stretch across ancient lunar lava plains in this close-up of the nearly full Beaver Moon captured from Nottingham, U.K. (Image credit: Daisy Dobrijevic) This striking image of the full moon rising above the Toronto skyline was snapped by Mert Alper Dervis as a flock of birds skimmed through the foreground. The outline of the lunar disk appears subtly warped and squashed by atmospheric refraction , as its reflected light passes through pockets of air with differing densities and temperatures. The moon rises into a pastel sky over Toronto. (Image credit: Photo by Mert Alper Dervis/Anadolu via Getty Images) Allen Berman sent in a breathtaking photo of the full moon hanging low over the Los Angeles skyline on the night of Nov. 24. "Finding the right spot for tonight’s full moon over downtown Los Angeles was a bit tricky," Berman told Space.com. "We wound up on a neighbor’s front lawn in the Baldwin Hills section of town. The owner was a bit surprised to see photographers there. But he was cool. The conditions were perfect with thin clouds over the distant mountains that made for a magical image." The November full moon shines over Los Angeles. (Image credit: Allen Berman) Moving from the modern to the old, photographer Robert Nemeti took a moody shot of the full Beaver Moon climbing skyward above the medieval Boldogkő Castle in Hungary at moonrise on Nov. 24. How many full moons must that old building have seen? An ancient castle broods below an older moon in Hungary. (Image credit: Photo by Robert Nemeti/Anadolu via Getty Images) Wang Zhao snapped a very different view from Beijing, China, on that same night by using a powerful telephoto lens to capture a passenger jet as it streaked across the lunar disk, leaving dense contrails in its wake. A passenger jet transits the lunar disk on Nov. 24. (Image credit: Photo by WANG Zhao / AFP via Getty Images) That Beaver Moon was captured shining between the minarets of the Imam Ali Shrine in the city of Najaf, Iraq, by Karar Essa. The 53-mile-wide (85-kilometer) Tycho Crater can be seen as a distinctive bright feature below the lunar equator, close to the dark expanse of Mare Nubium. Dark lunar seas mark the lunar disk as it glows in the skies over Iraq. (Image credit: Photo by Karar Essa/Anadolu via Getty Images) Aris Oikonomou snapped a striking photo of the Beaver Moon shining above the Parthenon in Athens, Greece, just as night began to set in over the Acropolis. The full Beaver Moon rises over the Parthenon in Athens, Greece. (Image credit: Photo by Aris Oikonomou / SOOC / AFP via Getty Images) Feeling inspired to capture your own supermoon photos? Then be sure to read our guide to photographing the moon and browse our picks of the best cameras and lenses for astrophotography because you don't have long to wait! The final supermoon of 2026 rises in just a few short weeks on Dec. 23 and it just so happens to be the closest full moon of the year, passing just 221,668 miles (356,740 kilometers) from Earth at the point of maximum illumination. So no excuses! We'd love to see your photo in our inbox next month. Editor's Note: If you would like to share your full moon photos with Space.com's readers, then please send your photo(s), comments, name and location to spacephotos@space.com.

item.title: Rust Will Officially Introduce Premium Paid Service With a Most-Requested Feature
item.description: In August, Facepunch removed the controversial Battle Pass system entry from this year's Rust roadmap. It was replaced with Rust Premium, a status that grants players who have at least $15 worth of items in their inventory access to premium servers , but not much else. This month's force wipe patch notes unveiled some additional details about the changes coming to Rust Premium "soon." As it turns out, Rust Premium will become a paid monthly service with exclusive perks and rewards.

item.title: Gatwick drop-off customers' personal data exposed in supplier breach
item.description: London Gatwick Airport has warned customers that a breach of its drop-off payment service exposed personal information and, in limited cases, payment records. A notification email seen by The Register identifies the affected system as AutoPay, operated by ParkPark and used by Gatwick's drop-off zone manager, Times24 UK Limited. AutoPay lets drivers register their vehicle and payment details in advance so drop-off charges are collected automatically. Gatwick told us it was unable to provide details about how many customers were affected by the breach, or how far back the affected records go. The email said most affected customers would have only some of the listed data exposed. The could include names, home addresses, cities, postcodes, contact details, and AutoPay login credentials such as email addresses and bcrypt-hashed passwords were affected. Other records implicated in the breach include details of vehicles linked to AutoPay accounts, those vehicles' entry and exit times at Times24-managed parking locations, and vehicle registrations. The email also states that payment records, including amounts, card types, card expiry dates, payment references, transaction statuses, transaction IDs, and drop-off locations and times were affected, but a Gatwick spokesperson said this applied only to "very limited cases." Again, in a minority of cases, "some limited emails between the customer service team and customers" were also exposed, the email stated. Gatwick said Times24 "immediately suspended" AutoPay after detecting the intrusion. The service remains disabled while the investigation continues. Airport officials are overseeing the response with outside cybersecurity specialists. Gatwick warned of possible disruption to its website but said flights were unaffected. Customers can still use Gatwick's drop-off zones, although they'll have to use alternative payment methods, and all other airport services are still operating as usual. The notification email urged customers to exercise caution when receiving communications from Gatwick, Times24, AutoPay, or ParkPark, especially those that ask for payment or bank details. Times24, which operates across more than 200 car parks in the UK, did not immediately respond to our request for more information. Dray Agha, senior manager at Huntress's tactical response division, warned that criminals could use the data for convincing scams long after news coverage of the breach has faded. "The real damage often comes after the breach," he said. "Criminals rarely use stolen data straight away; they'll wait until the headlines fade, then send a text about a 'parking fine' or an email offering a 'refund' that references a real booking. Even partial card details add a layer of credibility that makes people far more likely to hand over the rest. "Gatwick customers should assume any unexpected message about their parking could be a scam, check directly with the airport, and keep a close eye on their bank statements over the

Even partial card details add a layer of credibility that makes people far more likely to hand over the rest. "Gatwick customers should assume any unexpected message about their parking could be a scam, check directly with the airport, and keep a close eye on their bank statements over the coming months." ®

item.title: Microsoft declares ‘Code Red’ after huge Outlook outage
item.description: This month's Exchange Online and Microsoft Outlook outage has prompted the software giant to declare an unusual "Code Red" internally, Reuters reports . The nearly 24-hour outage took down email for millions of customers, and was triggered by a bug that had been sitting on Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers since July without any impact to servers. In a memo to the teams responsible for Exchange Online, Microsoft 365 Core president Jason Henderson revealed the outage was the most significant in history for Microsoft's customers. "Unfortunately, all the work we have done over the years was not sufficient to protect us on Thursday," said … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: Yemen's Houthis claim attacks on Riyadh financial district, Saudi refinery
item.description: Yemen's Houthis on Wednesday claimed attacks targeting the financial district in the Saudi capital and the sprawling Ras Tanura refinery in the kingdom's oil-rich east, in retaliation for strikes on their territory. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree described the attack targeting the refinery as "accurate and direct", saying it "caused fires to break out at the facility". He said the attack on Riyadh was "carried out in three phases, with strikes hitting their targets accurately".

item.title: Our ‘Paris manifesto’ proposes how to deal with extreme wealth in the AI age | Open letter
item.description: It is possible for democracy to reverse the dynamic of oligarchy. But we must act now The explosion of extreme wealth in the world is the defining social fact of our times. When Forbes magazine began ranking the world’s largest fortunes in 1987, the wealth of the richest 0.0001% of our planet’s population equaled 3% of global GDP. Since that time, the wealth held by this tiny group of people – just 3,000 households – has ballooned and now reaches 17% of global GDP. Continue reading...

item.title: Masobe Books and Narrative Landscape Announce Partnership to Bring Narrative Landscape Titles to Masobe App
item.description: Eghosa Imasuen, Managing Director of Narrative Landscape Press and Othuke Ominiabohs, Chief Executive Officer of Masobe Books Two of Nigeria’s foremost independent publishers, Masobe Books and Narrative Landscape Press, have announced a collaboration to bring Narrative Landscape’s titles to the Masobe App. The partnership marks a significant milestone for African literature, bringing some of the continent’s most celebrated literary works to a single, dedicated reading platform. Under the agreement, readers using the Masobe App, which was launched on 23rd March 2026, will soon be able to discover, purchase, and read titles from Narrative Landscape’s distinguished list alongside the existing Masobe Books catalogue. The integration brings together two complementary publishing houses whose lists have helped define contemporary Nigerian writing over the past decade, and represents one of the most ambitious cross-publisher digital initiatives in the African literary space to date. The collaboration is announced to address some of the most persistent challenges facing African readers and writers: discoverability, affordability and accessibility. By consolidating two of the country’s most respected catalogues onto a single, locally built platform, the partnership ensures African readers at home and across the diaspora can access a richer, deeper library of homegrown stories without the friction of fragmented distribution channels. “This collaboration is a statement of intent. African writing deserves world-class infrastructure, and by bringing Narrative Landscape’s exceptional catalogue onto the Masobe App, we are building exactly that. Together, we are creating a home where the best of our stories can live, be discovered, and be read,” said Othuke Ominiabohs , the Chief Executive Officer for Masobe Books. Narrative Landscape Press’s Managing Director, Eghosa Imasuen , said, “We have long believed that the future of African publishing depends on collaboration, not competition. Partnering with Masobe Books to make our titles available on the Masobe App means our authors will reach more readers, on a platform built with African readers at its core. This is a proud moment for everyone who believes in the power of our stories.” From the rollout date, Masobe App users can expect a phased introduction of Narrative Landscape titles spanning literary fiction, narrative non-fiction, romance, fantasy, contemporary fiction, among others. The expanded library will include works from a roster of acclaimed authors who have shaped the recent literary landscape in Nigeria and beyond, including Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie , Chimeka Garricks , Yejide Kilanko , Abubakar Adam Ibrahim , Chibundo Onuzo and Fatima Bala . The Masobe App, available on iOS and Android, has rapidly established itself as a leading destination for African literature, offering features tailored to local readers, including ebook, paperback and audiobook access; flexible payment options; reading goals and

item.title: The world's fastest computers have a problem: Keeping the work running
item.description: Frontier, Oak Ridge National Laboratory's exascale supercomputer, has thousands of processors working together on scientific problems. It also has a surprisingly ordinary way of ruining a researcher's day: one node going down. An uncorrectable memory error can do it, or a maintenance mishap. Scott Atchley , chief technology officer at the Oak Ridge Leadership Computing Facility, describes technicians accidentally rebooting the wrong node or risking a neighboring node's power supply while working in tightly packed racks. The hardware fault can affect just one node, but a simulation running across thousands of processors can grind to a halt. Then comes a series of questions. How recently did the application save its progress? How much computation needs repeating? And how long before the scheduler lets the job run again? For operators, the challenge isn't just keeping the supercomputer running. It's keeping the science moving. One bad node and everybody suffers On Frontier , a memory error can have an outsized audience. Atchley says uncorrectable double-bit errors in high-bandwidth memory occurred about 1.5 times a day during the supercomputer's early bring-up. Its predecessor, Summit, saw roughly one every two weeks. This sounds like a backward step, until you count the memory. Frontier has more than 16 times as much, giving bad bits considerably more places to hide. Memory isn't the only problem. Problematic GPU firmware can crash a node, and so can a technician rebooting the wrong one. Interconnect faults add another way for a large job to come unstuck. In a tightly coupled simulation using the Message Passing Interface (MPI) simulation, thousands of processes, or ranks, exchange data and participate in collective operations. If one rank disappears, the others cannot carry on as though nothing happened. Clockwork.io CEO Suresh Vasudevan describes a similar dependency in synchronized GPU training. One failed GPU can bring a 1,024-GPU job to a pause. An underperforming GPU can be almost as troublesome: if one participant runs at 80 percent speed, others might have to spend time waiting for it. The bigger the machine, the more ways there are for one small problem to become everybody's problem. How often should you hit save? Since stopping every component from failing isn't an option, researchers need a way to preserve their work. That's where checkpointing comes in. The application periodically saves its state so that, when something goes wrong, the simulation can resume from an earlier point instead of starting from scratch. The catch is that saving progress costs computing time, and doing it too often can become almost as wasteful as losing the work itself. Vasudevan explains this with an example. If writing a checkpoint takes 30 seconds, saving every five minutes consumes roughly 10 percent of computing time. Stretch that interval to 50 minutes, and the overhead drops to about 1 percent.
